			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our Board of Directors reviews the appropriateness of declaring or paying cash dividends on an ongoing basis. Any determination to declare or pay dividends in the future is at the discretion of our Board of Directors. Our Board of Directors takes into account such matters as general business conditions, our financial results, future prospects, capital requirements, contractual, legal and regulatory restrictions on the payment of dividends by us to our stockholders or by the Bank to the holding company, and such other factors as our Board of Directors may deem relevant. </font><font style="display: inline;">On February </font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors declared a quarterly stock dividend </font><font style="display: inline;">of 12 and &#xBD;</font><font style="display: inline;"> cents per share, payable </font><font style="display: inline;">on February 28, 2017 to stockholders of record on February 21, 2017.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">During 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> the Company paid stockholder dividends aggregating to 4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> cents per share. These dividends were paid at the level of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">11 and &#xBD; cents pe</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">r share, per quarter, in February, May, August and November 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. During 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> the Company paid stockholder dividends aggregating to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">0 cents per share. These dividends were paid at the level of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> cents per share, per quarter, in February, May, August and November 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our ability to pay dividends is subject to the restrictions of the Delaware General Corporation Law. Because we are a bank holding company with no significant assets other than our bank subsidiary, we currently depend upon dividends from the Bank for a substantial portion of our revenues. For further information on dividend restrictions affecting the Company and the Bank, refer to the discussion in the sub-sections titled &#x201C;Bank Holding Company Regulations Applicable to Guaranty Bancorp-Dividends&#x201D; and &#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Banking Regulations Applicable to Guaranty Bank-Dividends&#x201D; in Item 1, Business-Supervision and Regulation, and under Note 2(w) included</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> in the &#x201C;Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements&#x201D; contained in Part II, Item 8, &#x201C;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&#x201D;.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Under the terms of our trust preferred securities, including our related subordinated debentures, issued on June</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">30,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">2003 and April 8, 2004, we cannot declare or pay any dividends or distributions (other than stock dividends) on, or redeem, purchase, acquire or make a liquidation payment with respect to, any shares of our capital stock if (</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">i</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">)</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">an event of default under any of the subordinated debenture agreements has occurred and is continuing, or (</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ii</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">)</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">we defer payment of interest on the trust preferred securities (for a period of up to 60 consecutive months as long as we are in compliance with all covenants of the agreement). </font>

		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 8pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:8pt;">Return on average assets is determined by dividing net income </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:8pt;color:#000000;">(loss) by average assets.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 8pt;margin:0pt;">
				<sup style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:8pt;;"> (b)</sup>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 8pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:8pt;color:#000000;">Return on average stockholders&#x2019; equity is determined by dividing net income (loss) by average stockholders&#x2019; equity.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 8pt;margin:0pt;">
				<sup style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:8pt;;"> (c)</sup>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 8pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:8pt;color:#000000;">Net interest margin is determined by dividing net interest income by average interest-earning assets.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 8pt;margin:0pt;">
				<sup style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:8pt;;"> (d)</sup>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 8pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:8pt;color:#000000;">Efficiency ratio is determined by dividing total noninterest expense less intangible amortization expense, less select nonrecurring charges, by an amount equal to net interest income plus noninterest income, plus incremental tax benefit from tax exempt bonds and bank-owned life insurance.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Guaranty Bancorp is a bank holding company with its principal business to serve as the holding company for its Colorado-based bank subsidiary, Guaranty Bank and Trust Company (the &#x201C;Bank&#x201D;). The Bank is the sole member of several limited liability companies that hold real estate as well as the sole owner of two investment management firms, Private Capital Management LLC (&#x201C;PCM&#x201D;) and Cherry Hills Investment Advisors Inc. (&#x201C;CHIA&#x201D;). </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">On March 16, 2016, the Company entered into the Merger Agreement with Home State, the parent company of Home State Bank, a Colorado state chartered bank headquartered in Loveland, Colorado whereby Home State would merge into the Bank. The transaction closed on September 8, 2016 and substantially all integration activities were completed on November 7, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Through the Bank, we provide banking and other financial services throughout our targeted Colorado markets to small to medium-sized businesses, including the owners and employees of those businesses</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and consumers</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. Our banking products and services include accepting demand and time deposits and originating real estate loans (including construction loans), commercial loans, SBA guaranteed loans and consumer loans. The Bank, PCM and CHIA also provide wealth management solutions, including trust and investment management services. We derive our income primarily from interest (including loan origination fees) received on loans and, to a lesser extent, interest on investment securities and other fees received in connection with servicing loan and deposit accounts, trust and investment management services. Our major operating expenses include the interest we pay on deposits and borrowings and general operating expenses. We rely primarily on locally generated deposits to provide us with funds for making loans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;color:#000000;">In addition to building growth organically through our existing branches, we seek opportunities to acquire small to medium-sized banks or specialty finance companies that will allow us to expand our franchise in a manner consistent with our community-banking focus. Ideally, the financial institutions we seek to acquire will be in or contiguous to our existing footprint, which would allow us to use the acquisition to consolidate duplicative costs and administrative functions and to rationalize operating expenses. We believe that by streamlining the administrative and operational functions of an acquired financial institution, we are able to substantially lower operating costs, operate more efficiently and integrate the acquired financial institution while maintaining the stability of our existing business. In certain circumstances we may seek to acquire financial institutions that may be located outside of our existing footprint. We also seek opportunities which will allow us to further diversify our noninterest income base, including adding to our wealth management platform. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

In addition, the fiscal, monetary </font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Application of Critical Accounting Policies and Accounting Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our accounting policies are integral to understanding our reported financial results. Our most complex accounting policies require management&#x2019;s judgment to ascertain the valuation of assets, liabilities, commitments and contingencies. We have established detailed policies and procedures that are intended to ensure valuation methods are well controlled and consistently applied from period to period. In addition, the policies and procedures are intended to ensure that the process for changing methodologies occurs in an appropriate manner. The following is a brief description of our current accounting policies that we believe are critical or involve significant management judgment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Allowance for Loan Losses</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our loan portfolio represents the largest category of assets on our balance sheet. We estimate probable incurred losses in our loan portfolio and establish an allowance for those losses by considering factors including historical loss rates, expected cash flows and estimated collateral values. In assessing these factors, we use organizational history and experience with credit decisions and related outcomes. The allowance for loan losses represents our best estimate of losses inherent in the existing loan portfolio and is increased by the provision for loan losses charged to expense and reduced by credit provisions and loans charged off, net of recoveries. We evaluate our allowance for loan losses quarterly. If our underlying assumptions later prove to be inaccurate based on subsequent loss evaluations, we adjust the allowance for loan losses accordingly.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We estimate the appropriate level of allowance for loan losses by separately evaluating impaired and non-impaired loans. A specific allowance is assigned to an impaired loan when the present value of expected cash flows or value of underlying collateral does not support the carrying amount of the loan. The methodology used to assign an allowance to a non-impaired loan is more subjective. Generally, the allowance assigned to non-impaired loans is determined by applying historical loss rates by portfolio segment to existing loans with similar risk characteristics, adjusted for qualitative factors including the volume and types of loans we make, volume and severity of identified classified loans, economic conditions, changes in credit policies or underwriting standards, and changes in the level of credit risk associated with specific industries and markets. Because the economic and business climate in any given industry or market, and its impact on any given borrower, can change rapidly, management continually assesses the risk profile of our loan portfolio and adjusts it when appropriate. Despite the fact that we have these preventative procedures in place, there still exists the possibility that our assessment could prove to be incorrect and thus require an immediate adjustment to the allowance for loan losses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We estimate the appropriate level of loan loss allowance by conducting a detailed review of the three portfolio segments which comprise our loan portfolio. Loans in the same portfolio segment would normally have similar characteristics, such as risk classification, past due status, type of loan, industry or collateral. The risk profile of certain segments of the loan portfolio may be improving, while the risk profile of others may be deteriorating. As a result, an increase in the appropriate level of the allowance for one segment may offset a decrease for another. Adjustments to the allowance represent the aggregate impact from the analysis of each of our portfolio segments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Investment in Securities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We classify our investments in debt and equity securities as either held to maturity or available for sale. Securities classified as held to maturity are recorded at cost or amortized cost. Available for sale securities are carried at fair value. Fair value calculations are based on quoted market prices when such prices are available. If quoted market prices are not available, estimates of fair value are computed using a variety of techniques, including extrapolation from the quoted prices of similar instruments or recent trades for thinly traded securities, fundamental analysis, discounted cash flow analysis or through obtaining purchase quotes. Due to the subjective nature of the valuation process, it is possible that the actual fair values of these investments could differ from the estimated amounts, thereby affecting our financial position, results of operations and cash flows. If the estimated value of investments is less than the cost or amortized cost, we evaluate whether an event or change in circumstances has occurred that may have a significant adverse effect on the fair value of the investment. If such an event or change has occurred and we determine that the impairment is other-than-temporary, we expense the impairment of the investment in the period in which the event or change occurred.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Business Combinations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company accounts for acquisitions of businesses using the acquisition method of accounting. Under the acquisition method, assets acquired and liabilities assumed are recorded at their estimated fair value upon the date of acquisition. Management utilizes </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">third party valuation, such as appraisals which incorporate </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">various valuation techniques including discounted cash flow analyses to determine the fair values of assets acquired and liabilities assumed. Any excess of purchase price over amounts allocated to the acquired assets, including identifiable intangible assets, and liabilities assumed is recorded as goodwill. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 3pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:3pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company&#x2019;s net income for 2016 increased by $2.3 million to $24.7 million compared to $22.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2015. Earnings per basic common share decreased to $1.06 and earnings per diluted common share </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">de</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">creased to $1.05 for the year ended December 31, 2016 compared to $1.07 per basic common share and $1.06 per diluted common share for the year ended December 31, 2015.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The increase in net income for 2016, compared to 2015, was</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> due to a $13.4 million increase in net interest income and a $2.1 million increase in noninterest income, partially offset by a $12.4 million increase in noninterest expense and an increase in income taxes due to higher pretax income. The $13.4 million increase in net interest income for the year ended December 31, 2016, compared to 2015, was comprised of a $17.5 million increase in interest income, primarily due to a $411.3 million, or a 19.6% increase in average earnings assets, partially offset by a $4.1 million increase in interest expense mostly due to a $299.9 million, or 26.8% increase in average interest bearing deposits. The $2.1 million increase in noninterest income for the year ended December 31, 2016, compared to 2015, was mostly related to a $1.5 million increase in deposit services and other fees and a $0.3 million increase in investment </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">management </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and trust fees. Noninterest expense increased $12.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2016, compared to the same period in 2015, mostly due to $6.3 million in merger-related expenses incurred in 2016. The $6.3 million in merger-related expenses included $1.9 million in severance, retention bonuses and related taxes and $4.4 million in other general and administrative expense, consisting of professional fees and system conversion costs. Excluding </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the $1.9 million in severance, retention bonuses and related taxes, described above, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">salaries and employee benefits</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> expense </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">increased $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">5.5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million during 2016 as compared to 2015, primarily due to the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">addition</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of 143 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">full-time equivalent employees</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, mostly due to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">employees added pursuant to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the Home State transaction</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>

The increase in the Company&#x2019;s total risk-based capital ratio was primarily due to an increase in capital related to the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Home State transaction</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, in addition t</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">o growth in retained earnings. </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2015 Compared to 2014</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company&#x2019;s net income for 2015 increased by $8.9 million to $22.5 million compared to $13.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2014. Earnings per basic common share increased to $1.07 and earnings per diluted common share increased to $1.06 for the year ended December 31, 2015 compared to $0.64 per basic and diluted common share for the year ended December 31, 2014. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The increase in net income in 2015, compared to 2014, was attributable to a $6.8 million increase in interest income, a $1.4 million decrease in interest expense, a $0.5 million increase in noninterest income and a $5.4 million decrease in noninterest expense. These improvements were partially offset by a $5.0 million increase in income taxes as a result of the Company&#x2019;s increased pretax income. The $6.8 million increase in interest income was the result of a $236.4 million increase in average loans for the year ended December 31, 2015 compared to the year ended December 31, 2014. The decline in interest expense during 2015, compared to the prior year, was primarily due to the prepayment of $90.0 million in Federal Home Loan Bank (&#x201C;FHLB&#x201D;) term advances in the fourth quarter 2014. The $0.5 million increase in noninterest income was mostly due to a $0.8 million increase in investment management and trust income for the year ended December 31, 2015 compared to the same period in 2014. The $5.4 million decrease in noninterest expense for the year ended December 31, 2015 compared to the year ended December 31, 2014 was primarily due to the $5.5 million penalty incurred in the fourth quarter 2014 as a result of the prepayment of $90.0 million in FHLB term advances.</font>
		</p>

The decrease in the Company&#x2019;s total risk-based capital ratio was primarily due to an increase in risk-weighted assets attributable to loan growth during 2015.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Net interest income, which is our primary source of income, represents the difference between interest earned on assets and interest paid on liabilities.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The interest rate spread is the difference between the yield on our interest-bearing assets and liabilities. Net </font><font style="display: inline;">interest margin is net interest income expressed as a percentage of average interest-earning assets.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

</div>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"> Compared to 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">5</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">For the year ended December 31, 2016, the Company&#x2019;s net interest income increased by $13.4&nbsp;million to $90.4 million compared to $77.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2015. This increase in net interest income during 2016</font><font style="display: inline;"> was attributable to a</font><font style="display: inline;"> $14.6 million favorable volume variance partially offset by a $1.2 million unfavorable rate variance.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The favorable volume variance of $14.6 million in 2016</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> compared to 2015</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> was primarily the result of a $16.4&nbsp;million favorable volume variance related to average earning assets partially offset by a $1.8&nbsp;million unfavorable volume variance on average interest-bearing liabilities. The favorable volume variance in average interest-earning assets was mostly attributable to a $368.9 million increase in average loan</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. The unfavorable volume variance in average interest-bearing liabilities was attributable to a $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">299.9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million increase in average interest-bearing deposits and a $20.7 million increase in average borrowings.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The $1.2 million unfavorable rate variance in 2016, compared to 2015</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> was the result of an unfavorable rate variance of $2.3 million related to average interest-bearing liabilities, partially offset by a favorable rate variance of $1.1&nbsp;million related to average interest earning assets. The unfavorable rate variance in average interest-bearing </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">l</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">iabilities was primarily due to a 66 basis point increase in average yield on borrowings, a 143 basis point increase in the average yield on subordinated debentures </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">a &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">five</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> basis point increase in yield on interest-bearing </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">deposits. The $1.1 million favorable rate variance on interest earning assets </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">was</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> primarily attributable to $1.3 million in accretion of the discount on loans acquired in the Home State transaction</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">The following table presents the dollar amount of changes in interest income and interest expense for the major categories of our interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. Information is provided for each category of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities with respect to (i) changes attributable to volume (i.e., changes in average balances multiplied by the prior-period average rate) and (ii) changes attributable to rate (i.e., changes in average rate multiplied by prior-period average balances). For purposes of this table, changes attributable to both rate and volume, which cannot be segregated, have been allocated proportionately to the change due to volume and the change due to rate.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">For the year ended December 31, 2015, the Company&#x2019;s net interest income increased by $8.2&nbsp;million to $77.0</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">million compared to $68.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2014. This increase in net interest income during 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> was attributable to a</font><font style="display: inline;">n</font><font style="display: inline;"> $8.3 million favorable volume variance partially offset by a $0.2 million unfavorable rate variance.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The favorable volume variance of $8.3 million in 2015 compared to 2014 was primarily the result of a $9.5&nbsp;million favorable volume variance related to average earning assets partially offset by a $1.2&nbsp;million unfavorable volume variance on </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">average </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">interest</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">-</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">bearing liabilities. The favorable volume variance in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">average </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">interest-earning assets was mostly attributable to a $236.4 million increase in average loan balances, partially offset by an $18.4 million decrease in average investments. The unfavorable volume variance in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">average </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">interest-bearing liabilities was attributable to a $122.1 million increase in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">average </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">interest-bearing deposits and a $28.7 million increase in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">average </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">borrowings. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The $0.2 million unfavorable rate variance in 2015, compared to 2014 was the result of an unfavorable rate variance</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of $2.7 million related to average </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">earning assets, partially offset by a favorable rate variance of $2.5&nbsp;million related to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">average</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> interest-bearing liabilities. The unfavorable rate variance in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">average </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">earning assets was primarily due to a 19 basis point decline in average loan yield</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. The decline in loan yield</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> was primarily due to lower rates on new and renewing loans, which had a more pronounced impact due to the 17.7% loan growth recognized during 2015, and reflect</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ed</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> the extremely </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">competitive interest rate environment. The unfavorable rate variance in average earning assets was partially offset by a 17 basis point decline in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the average</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> cost of funds during the year, from 0.56% in 2014 to 0.39% in 2015. This decline was mostly due to the December 2014 prepayment of $90.0 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in FHLB term advances as discussed above. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">P</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">rovision for Loan Losses</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The provision for loan losses </font><font style="display: inline;">is </font><font style="display: inline;">a charge against earnings</font><font style="display: inline;"> and represents management&#x2019;s estimate of </font><font style="display: inline;">the amount required to maintain the allowance for loan losses at a level that, in our judgment, is adequate to absorb probable incurred loan losses in the loan portfolio. The provision for loan losses is based on our allowance methodology and reflects our judgments about the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses. In determining the amount of the provision, we consider certain quantitative and qualitative factors, including our historical loan loss experience, the volume and type of lending we conduct, the results of our credit review process, the amounts and severity of classified, criticized and nonperforming assets, regulatory policies, general economic conditions, underlying collateral values and other factors regarding collectability and impairment.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The </font><font style="display: inline;">estimated </font><font style="display: inline;">amount of expected loss </font><font style="display: inline;">in</font><font style="display: inline;"> our loan portfolio is influenced by the collateral value associated with our loans. Loans with greater collateral values</font><font style="display: inline;">, as a percentage of the outstanding loan balance, reduce</font><font style="display: inline;"> our exposure to loan loss provision.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For further discussion of the methodology and factors impacting management&#x2019;s estimate of the allowance for loan losses, see &#x201C;Financial Condition &#x2013; Allowance for Loan Losses&#x201D; below. For a discussion of impaired loans and associated collateral values, see &#x201C;Financial Condition&#x2014;Nonperforming Assets and Other Impaired Loans&#x201D; below. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Compared to 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">5</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The provision for loan losses was $0.1 million in both 2016 and 2015. </font><font style="display: inline;">The $0.1 million provision recognized in 2016 was impacted by an increase of $0.3 million </font><font style="display: inline;">in </font><font style="display: inline;">the general </font><font style="display: inline;">component of our allowance for loan losses</font><font style="display: inline;">, a $0.1 million decline in the specific component of our allowance for loan losses and by $0.1 million in net recoveries. </font><font style="display: inline;">The increase in the general component of the allowance for loan losses was primarily attributable to the growth in loans during 2016. During 2016, net recoveries were $0.1 million, compared to $0.4 million in net recoveries during 2015. The Company determined that the provision for loan losses recorded during 2016 was necessary to maintain the allowance for loan losses at an adequate level for the probable incurred losses in the loan portfolio as of December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2016.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As a percentage of loans, the allowance for loan losses decreased to 0.92% at December 31, 2016, compared to 1.27% at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2015. The decrease in the allowance as a percentage of total loans during 2016 compared to the prior year was primarily the result of the acquisition </font><font style="display: inline;">of $445.5 </font><font style="display: inline;">million in loans in the Home State transaction, for which no allowance was established as of the date of acquisition </font><font style="display: inline;">in accordance with</font><font style="display: inline;"> GAAP. </font><font style="display: inline;">When the unaccreted purchase discount is added to the allowance for loan losses, the combined allowance and purchase discount was 1.</font><font style="display: inline;">50% of loans held for investment as of December 31, 2016. The ratio of allowance for loan losses to nonperforming loans </font><font style="display: inline;">and purchased discount </font><font style="display: inline;">increased to 722.93% at December 31, 2016 from 158.91% at December 31, 2015, primarily as a result of a $9.4 million out-of-state loan syndication </font><font style="display: inline;">returning </font><font style="display: inline;">t</font><font style="display: inline;">o performing status during the third quarter 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Compared to 2014</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The provision for loan losses was $0.1 million in 2015 compared to an immaterial provision for loan losses in 2014. </font><font style="display: inline;">The $0.</font><font style="display: inline;">1</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">million </font><font style="display: inline;">provision recognized in 2015 was impacted by increases of $0.4 million and $0.1 million to the general and specific components of our allowance for loan losses, offset by $0.4 million in net recoveries. The increase in the general component of the allowance for loan losses was primarily attributable to the growth in loans during 2015. During 2015, net recoveries were $0.4 million, as compared to $1.5 million in net recoveries during 2014. The Company determined that the provision for loan losses recorded during 2015 was necessary to maintain </font><font style="display: inline;">the </font><font style="display: inline;">allowance for loan losses at an adequate level for the probable incurred losses in the loan portfolio as of December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As a </font><font style="display: inline;">percentage of loans, </font><font style="display: inline;">the</font><font style="display: inline;"> allowance </font><font style="display: inline;">for loan losses </font><font style="display: inline;">decreased to 1.27% at December 31, 2015, as compared to 1.46% at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2014. The decrease in the allowance as a percentage of total loans during 2015 as compared to the prior year was the result of </font><font style="display: inline;">a reduction in the historical loss rate utilized to estimate current incurred losses in the loan portfolio</font><font style="display: inline;">. The ratio of allowance for loan losses to nonperforming loans </font><font style="display: inline;">de</font><font style="display: inline;">creased to 158.91% at December 31, 2015 from 178.25% at December 31, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, primarily as a result of a net $1.9 million increase in nonperforming loans</font><font style="display: inline;">, attributable to three loans with an aggregate principal balance of $2.7 million, </font><font style="display: inline;">which </font><font style="display: inline;">were moved to </font><font style="display: inline;">nonaccrual status during 2015</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"> Compared to 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">5</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The effective tax rate in 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> was 32.7% compared to 33.4% in 2015. In 2016, the primary differences between the statutory rate of approximately 38.0% and the effective tax rate were tax-exempt income and state taxes. The decrease in the effective tax rate during 2016</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> compared to 2015 was the result of tax-exempt income in 2016 representing a slightly greater proportion of pretax income compared to 2015, due in part to the Home State transaction. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company adopted the provisions of the</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">accounting standards update 2016-09 Compensation-Stock Compensation</font><font style="display: inline;"> in the fourth quarter of 2016 with the most significant impact being $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.5 million </font><font style="display: inline;">of excess tax benefit in restricted stock vestings directly benefiting 2016 income tax expense.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">For further information regarding differences between the effective tax rate and the actual tax rate, see Note&nbsp;1</font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;">, Income Taxes </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">under Item 8. &#x201C;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data &#x2013; Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements&#x201D;.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Income tax expense is the total of the current year income tax due or refundable and the change in deferred tax assets and liabilities. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases and operating loss and tax credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date. Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when, in the opinion of management, it is more likely than not that some portion, or all, of the deferred tax asset will not be realized. In assessing the realizability of deferred tax assets, management evaluates both positive and negative evidence, including the existence of any cumulative losses in the current year and the prior two years, the amount of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">taxes paid in available carry-back years, forecasts of future income, applicable tax planning strategies, and assessments of current and future economic and business conditions. This analysis is updated quarterly and adjusted as necessary.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">2015 Compared to 2014</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended December 31, 2015 income tax expense of $11.3 million was recognized compared to $6.2 million recognized in the year ending December 31, 2014. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The effective tax rate in 2015 was 33.4% compared to 31.6% in 2014. In 2015, the primary differences between the statutory rate of approximately 38.0% and the effective tax rate were tax-exempt income and state taxes. The increase in the effective tax rate during 2015 compared to 2014 was the result of tax-exempt income in 2015 representing a slightly smaller proportion of pretax income compared to 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Financial Condition </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2016, the Company had total assets of $3.4 billion, compared to $2.4 billion at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2015, representing a year-over-year increase of $997.9 million. </font><font style="display: inline;">The increase in total assets year-over-year was comprised of a $704.6 million increase in loans, a $166.2 million increase in investments and a $66.5&nbsp;million increase in goodwill and intangible assets. </font><font style="display: inline;">The increase in total assets was primarily funded by an </font>

Borrowers have the right to prepay their loans with or without penalty, based on their specific loan agreement provisions. Demand </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">notes </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">or other loans having no stated maturity and no stated schedule of repayments are reported as due in one year or less. The table also presents, for loans with maturities over one year, an analysis with respect to fixed interest rate loans and floating interest </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">rate loans. The table excludes</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">deferred costs and fees </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">and loans held for sale</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>

				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:01.66%;border-top:1pt solid #000000 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:2pt double #000000 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;height:10.50pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:right;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
						<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">$</font></p>
				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:10.34%;border-top:1pt solid #000000 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:2pt double #000000 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;height:10.50pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;text-align:right;" nowrap="nowrap">810,697&nbsp;

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">N</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">onperforming Assets and Other Impaired Loans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Credit risk related to nonperforming assets </font><font style="display: inline;">is inherent in</font><font style="display: inline;"> lending activities.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">To manage this risk, we </font><font style="display: inline;">utilize routine </font><font style="display: inline;">monitoring procedures and take prompt corrective action when necessary. We employ a risk rating system that identifies the potential risk associated with loans in our loan portfolio. This monitoring and rating system is designed to help management </font><font style="display: inline;">identify</font><font style="display: inline;"> current and potential problems so that corrective actions can be taken promptly.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Generally, loans are placed on nonaccrual status when they become 90 days or more past due or at such earlier time as management determines timely recognition of interest to be in doubt. Accrual of interest is discontinued on a loan when we believe, after considering economic and business conditions and analysis of the borrower&#x2019;s financial condition and the underlying collateral value, that the collection of interest is doubtful.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">A loan is impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that we will be unable to collect </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the scheduled payments when</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> due according to the contractual terms of the</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> underlying</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> loan agreement. Impaired loans consist of our nonaccrual loans, loans that are 90 days or more past due, and other loans for which we determine that noncompliance with contractual terms of the loan agreement is probable. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Losses on individually identified impaired loans that are not collateral dependent are measured based on the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the original effective interest rate of each loan. For loans that are collateral dependent, impairment is measured based on the fair value of the collateral less estimated selling costs. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">At December 31, 2016, nonperforming assets had decreased $9.3 million to $5.8 million from $15.1 million at December 31, 2015. The $9.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">3</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million decrease in nonperforming assets as of December 31, 2016, compared to December 31, 2015, was primarily the result of a single out-of-state syndication of $9.4 million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">returning</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to performing status in the third quarter 2016. </font>
		</p>

At December 31, 2015, nonperforming loans were primarily comprised of approximately $11.9 million in commercial real estate loans.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our loss exposure on nonperforming loans is mitigated by collateral positions on these loans. The allocated allowance for loan losses associated with impaired loans is computed based upon the related collateral value of the loans if the loan is collateral-dependent or based on the present value of expected cash flows if the loan does not qualify as collateral-dependent. The collateral values are determined by recent appraisals, but are generally discounted by management based on historical collateral dispositions, changes in market conditions since the last valuation, and management&#x2019;s expertise and knowledge of the client and the client&#x2019;s business. Management reviews all real estate loan relationships in excess of $500,000 annually, or more frequently where risk categories or property conditions suggest a potentially significant decline in the property&#x2019;s value. If management determines that such a decline exists, we obtain an updated appraisal. Similarly, upon the renewal, extension or refinancing of a real estate loan, we obtain an appraisal when management determines that there has been a significant decline in value. Appraisals are required in compliance with bank policy and applicable regulations. Generally speaking, appraisals are required for all new commercial real estate loans or loans secured by residential property in excess of $250,000; new business loans secured by real estate in excess of $1.0 million; renewals, extensions or refinancing with the advance of new monies if there is evidence of market or property deterioration; and any foreclosure of other real estate in excess of $250,000. If an appraisal is not required, an internal evaluation </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">is completed </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">or other alternative re-valuation approach </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">is </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">used</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">As further described below under &#x201C;Allowance for Loan Losses&#x201D; we categorize</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> loans into risk categories based on relevant information </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">obtained regarding </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the ability of borrowers to service their debt, such as current financial information, historical payment experience, credit documentation, public information, and current economic trends, among other factors. These risk categories are based on the definitions in the Uniform Agreement on the Classification of Assets and Appraisal of Securities Held by Banks and Thrifts issued by the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">OCC</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">FDIC </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Each internal risk classification is judgmental, but based on objective and subjective factors/criteria. As described below under &#x201C;Allowance for Loan Losses&#x201D;, the Company adjusts the general component of its allowance for loan losses for the trends in the volume and severity of adversely classified loans.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">At December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, the amount of loans that the Company has internally considered to be adversely classified, other than impaired </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">loans, increased to $6.2 million</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> compared to $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.5 million at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">; $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">2.5 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">million at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">4; $5.7</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">3 and $24.3 million at December 31, 2012.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Allowance for Loan Losses </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The allowance for loan losses is maintained at a level that, in our judgment, is adequate to absorb probable incurred loan losses in the loan portfolio. The amount of the allowance is based on management&#x2019;s evaluation of the collectability of the loan portfolio, historical loss experience and other significant factors affecting loan portfolio collectability, including the level and trends in delinquent, nonaccrual and adversely classified loans, trends in volume and terms of loans, levels and trends in credit concentrations, effects of changes in underwriting standards, policies, procedures and practices, national and local economic trends and conditions, changes in capabilities and experience of lending management and staff and other external factors including industry conditions, competition and regulatory requirements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our methodology for evaluating the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses has two basic elements: first, the specific identification of impaired loans and the measurement of an estimated loss for each individual loan identified; and second, estimating a nonspecific allowance for probable losses on all other loans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The specific allowance for impaired loans and the allowance calculated for probable incurred losses on other loans are combined to determine the required allowance for loan losses. The amount calculated is compared to the recorded allowance balance at each quarter end and any shortfall is charged against income as an additional provision for loan losses.</font><font style="display: inline;"> If the amount calculated exceeds the recorded allowance for loan losses, the excess would be credited to income as a credit provision for loan losses.</font><font style="display: inline;"> For further discussion of the </font><font style="display: inline;">provision</font><font style="display: inline;"> for loan losses, see &#x201C;Provision for Loan Losses&#x201D; above.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In estimating the allowance for probable incurred losses on other loans, we group the balance of the loan portfolio into </font><font style="display: inline;">portfolio </font><font style="display: inline;">segments that have common characteristics, such as loan type or risk rating. For each nonspecific allowance portfolio segment, we apply loss factors to calculate the required allowance based upon actual historical loss rates </font><font style="display: inline;">over a time period that we have determined represents the current credit cycle, </font><font style="display: inline;">adjusted for qualitative factors affecting loan portfolio collectability as described above. </font><font style="display: inline;">We</font><font style="display: inline;"> also look</font><font style="display: inline;"> at r</font><font style="display: inline;">i</font><font style="display: inline;">sk ratings of loans and compute</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;a</font><font style="display: inline;"> qualitative adjustment based on our credit quality in consideration of credit quality during the historical loss </font><font style="display: inline;">period. We also consider other qualitative factors that may warrant adjustment of the computed historical loss rate, including loan growth, loan concentrations, economic considerations and organizational factors. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We monitor</font><font style="display: inline;"> the allowance for loan losses closely and adjust the allowance when necessary, based on </font><font style="display: inline;">our</font><font style="display: inline;"> analysis, which includes an ongoing evaluation of </font><font style="display: inline;">impaired</font><font style="display: inline;"> loans and their collateral positions</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">61</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">At December 31, 2016, the allowance for loan losses was $23.3 million, or 0.92% of total loans held for investment. This compares to an allowance for loan losses of $23.0 million, or 1.27% of total loans held for investment at December 31, 2015. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The $0.3 million increase in the allowance for loan losses during 2016 was primarily a result of the additional reserves needed on the net increase in loans of $700.5 million. The additional reserves attributed to growth in loans were partially offset by a decline in reserves tied to historical losses given the net recoveries recognized in 2016. Charge-offs are taken on loans when management determines, after review of all possible sources of repayment including future cash flows, collateral values and the financial strength of guarantors or co-makers, that there is no longer a reasonable probability that the principal can be collected.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Net charge-offs have an impact on the historical loss component of our allowance for loan losses computation. We utilize a history of net charge-offs, incurred during the current credit cycle, to calculate our historical loss rate</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> which is adjusted as necessary by management in consideration of various qualitative factors.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Approximately $0.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, or 1.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">%, of the $23.3 million allowance for loan losses at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2016, relates to specific reserve allocations. This compares to a specific reserve of $0.3 million, or 1.3%, of the total </font>

The evaluated pricing models apply available information as applicable through processes such as benchmark curves, benchmarking of like securities, sector groupings and matrix pricing. These models assess interest rate impact, develop prepayment scenarios and take into account market conventions. Standard inputs into these models include benchmark yields, reported trades, broker/dealer quotes, issuer spreads, two-sided markets, benchmark securities, bids, offers and reference data including market research publications.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Borrowings </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
