		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Subordinated Debentures and Trust Preferred Securities </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In April 2004, a predecessor to the Company formed CenBank Statutory Trust III and the trust completed an offering of $15.0 million, LIBOR plus 2.65% Cumulative </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Trust Preferred Securities (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">TruPS</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, which are guaranteed by the Company. The trust also issued common securities to the predecessor of the Company and used the net proceeds from the offering to purchase $15.5 million in principal amount of floating rate Junior Subordinated Debentures (&#x201C;Debentures&#x201D;) issued by the predecessor. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company assumed the predecessor&#x2019;s obligations relating to such securities upon the acquisition of the predecessor. Interest paid on the Debentures was distributed to the holders of the TruPS. Distributions payable on the TruPS were recorded as interest expense in the consolidated statements of income. These Debentures were unsecured, ranked junior and were subordinate in right of payment to all senior debt of the Company. The TruPS were subject to mandatory redemption upon repayment of the Debentures. The Company had the right, subject to events of default, to defer payments of interest on the Debentures at any time by extending the interest payment period for a period not exceeding 10 consecutive semi-annual periods with respect to each deferral period, provided that no extension period could extend beyond the redemption or maturity date of the Debentures.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> The Debentures mature on April&nbsp;15,&nbsp;2034 and are callable on each quarterly payment date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In June 2003, a predecessor to the Company formed Guaranty Capital Trust III and the trust completed an offering of $10.0 million, LIBOR plus 3.10% Cumulative TruPS which are guaranteed by the Company. The trust also issued common securities to the predecessor of the Company and used the net proceeds from the offering to purchase $10.3 million in principal amount of junior subordinated debentures issued by the predecessor. The Company assumed the predecessor&#x2019;s obligations relating to such securities upon the acquisition of the predecessor. Interest is paid quarterly and is distributed to the holders of the TruPS. The other terms and condition</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of these Debentures are substantially similar to those as described under the CenBank Statutory Trust III. The Debentures mature on July 7, 2033 and are callable on each quarterly interest payment date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the terms of each indenture, we have the ability to defer interest on the debentures for a period of up to 60 months as long as we are in compliance with all covenants of the agreement. At December 31, 2016, the interest payments with respect to our two subordinated debentures were current.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company is not considered the primary beneficiary of these trusts (variable interest entities), therefore the trusts are not consolidated in the Company&#x2019;s financial statements, but rather the subordinated debentures are shown as a liability. The Company&#x2019;s investment in the common stock of each trust is included in other assets on the consolidated balance sheets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the Dodd-Frank Act and the joint rule from the Federal Reserve Board, the OCC and the FDIC, certain TruPS are no longer eligible to be included as Tier 1 capital for regulatory purposes. However, an exception to this statutory prohibition applies to securities issued prior to May 19, 2010 by bank holding companies with less than $15 billion of total assets. As we have less than $15 billion in total assets and issued all of our TruPS prior to May&nbsp;19,&nbsp;2010, we expect our TruPS will continue to be eligible to be treated as Tier 1 capital, subject to other rules and limitations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">In July 2016, the Company issued $40.0 million in fixed-floating rate subordinated debentures primarily to fund the cash consideration paid to Home State shareholders in the Home State transaction.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> The subordinated debentures bear a fixed interest rate of 5.75% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears. On July 20, 2021 and thereafter the interest on the subordinated debentures will be payable quarterly in arrears, at an annual floating rate equal to three-month LIBOR as determined by the applicable quarterly period, plus 4.73%. The subordinated debentures mature on July 20, 2026.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Although the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">subordinated debt is</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> not included as a component of stockholders&#x2019; equity on the consolidated balance sheets, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">it</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">is</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> treated as capital for regulatory purposes. Specifically, under applicable regulatory guidelines, the Company is allowed to include in Tier 1 capital an amount of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">subordinated debt </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">equal to no more than 25% of the sum of all core capital elements, which is generally defined as stockholders&#x2019; equity less certain intangibles, including core deposit intangibles and customer relationship intangibles, net of any related deferred income tax liability. Any amount that exceeds 25% qualifies as Tier 2 capital. At December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2016, $</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">25.0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">subordinated debt qualified as Tier 1 capital and $40.0 million of subordinated debt qualified as Tier 2 capital.</font>

As a result of the prepayment, the Company incurred a prepayment penalty of approximately $5.5 million.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>

The third fixed-rate term note is a </font><font style="display: inline;">$20.0 million</font><font style="display: inline;"> note</font><font style="display: inline;"> matur</font><font style="display: inline;">ing</font><font style="display: inline;"> on January 23, 2018 with an interest rate of 2.52% and is convertible on a quarterly basis by the FHLB to a variable rate </font><font style="display: inline;">note.</font><font style="display: inline;"> If the note is converted by the FHLB, we have the option to prepay the </font><font style="display: inline;">note</font><font style="display: inline;"> without penalty.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The two variable-rate term notes of $25.0 million each bore</font><font style="display: inline;"> interest rate</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> of 0.96% </font><font style="display: inline;">and 1.15% at December 31, 2016. These notes </font><font style="display: inline;">mature on March 7, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;"> and August 4, 2017 and</font><font style="display: inline;"> will be renewed annually for the next four years under our five year forward starting balance sheet swaps initiated in June 201</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;"> and March 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

The Bank ha</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">d</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> additional borrowing capacity </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">with FHLB </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of $400.1 million at December 31, 2016, which can be utilized with term advances, line of credit advances or a combination of both.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

As of December 31, 2016 no amounts had been borrowed on this line of credit.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Current risk-based regulatory capital standards generally require banks and bank holding companies to maintain a ratio of Common Equity Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets of at least 4.50%, </font><font style="display: inline;">a ratio of </font><font style="display: inline;">Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets of at least 6.00%, a ratio of Tier 1 capital to average total assets (leverage ratio) of at least 4.00% and a ratio of total capital (which includes Tier 1 capital plus certain forms of subordinated debt, a portion of the allowance for loan and lease losses, and preferred stock) to risk-weighted assets of at least 8.00%. </font><font style="display: inline;">However, u</font><font style="display: inline;">nder the final rule on Enhanced Regulatory Capital Standards, commonly referred to as Basel III, which became effective in the first quarter 2015, a capital conservation buffer of 2.5%, comprised of Common Equity Tier 1, was established above the regulatory minimum capital requirement. The capital conservation buffer phase-in period began January 1, 2016 and will become fully effective on January 1, 2019. A fully phased-in capital conservation buffer is included in the table below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Bank made the one-time accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) (&#x201C;AOCI&#x201D;) opt-out election on its March 31, 2015 Call Report, which allowed community banks under $250 billion, in total assets, which made the one-time opt-out election, to remove the impact of certain unrealized gains and losses from the calculation of regulatory capital. There is no opportunity to change methodology in future periods.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2016, all of our regulatory capital ratios remain well above minimum requirements for a &#x201C;well-capitalized&#x201D; institution. </font><font style="display: inline;">Our consolidated Common Equity Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio, our Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio and our leverage ratio declined compared to December 31, 2015, while our consolidated total risk-based capital ratio increased during the same period. </font><font style="display: inline;">Our consolidated capital ratios were impacted by the Home State transaction in the third quarter 2016. </font><font style="display: inline;">The</font><font style="display: inline;"> Home State transaction was funded through the issuance of $40.0 million in fixed-to-floating rate subordinated notes, which qualified for treatment as Tier 2 capital, and by the issuance of common stock valued at $117.5 million, which qualified as Common Equity Tier 1 capital. </font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Bank relies on deposits as its principal source of funds</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and therefore must be in a position to service depositors&#x2019; needs as they arise. Fluctuations in the </font><font style="display: inline;">account </font><font style="display: inline;">balances of a few large depositors may cause temporary increases and decreases in liquidity from time to time. We deal with such fluctuations by using </font><font style="display: inline;">other sources of </font><font style="display: inline;">liquidity</font><font style="display: inline;">, as discussed below</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Bank&#x2019;s initial sources of liquidity are its liquid assets. At December 31, 2016, the Company had</font><font style="display: inline;"> $328.9&nbsp;million in unencumbered securities, $50.1 million in cash and cash equivalents and $24.9 </font><font style="display: inline;">million of excess pledging related to customer accounts that required collateral. When the level of our liquid assets does not meet our liquidity needs, other available sources of liquid assets, includ</font><font style="display: inline;">ing</font><font style="display: inline;"> the purchase of federal funds, sales of loans, including jumbo mortgage loans, brokered and internet certificates of deposit, one-way purchases of certificates of deposit through the Certificates of Deposit Account Registry Service, discount window borrowings from the Federal Reserve and our lines of credit with the FHLB and other correspondent banks are employed to meet current and presently anticipated funding needs</font><font style="display: inline;">. At December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2016, the Bank had approximately $400.1 million of availability on its FHLB line, $50.8&nbsp;million of availability on its unsecured federal funds lines with correspondent banks and $3.3&nbsp;million of availability with the Federal Reserve discount window.</font>
		</p>

We continue to evaluate new brokered deposits as a source of low-cost, longer-term </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">funding.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The holding company relies primarily on cash flow from the Bank as its source of liquidity. The holding company requires liquidity for the payment of interest on the subordinated debentures, for operating expenses, principally salaries and benefits, for repurchases of our common stock and, if declared by our Board of Directors, for the payment of dividends to our stockholders. The Bank pays a management fee for its share of expenses paid by the holding company, as well as for services provided by the holding company. As discussed in the &#x201C;Capital Resources&#x201D; section above, v</font><font style="display: inline;">arious banking laws applicable to the Bank limit the payment of dividends by the Bank to the holding company, and may therefore limit our ability to pay dividends on our common stock. Under these laws, the Bank is currently required to request permission from the Federal Reserve prior to payment of a dividend to the Company. Under the terms of our TruPS financings, we may defer payment of interest on the subordinated debentures and related TruPS for a period of up to 60 consecutive months as long as we are in compliance with all covenants of the agreement.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 2016, the holding company had approximately $9.5 million of cash on hand. Based on current cash flow projections for the holding company, we estimate that cash balances maintained by the holding company are sufficient to meet the operating needs of the holding </font><font style="display: inline;">company through 2019</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Dividends </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Holders of voting common stock are entitled to dividends out of funds legally available for such dividends, when, and if, declared by the Board of Directors. Beginning in May 2013, we paid cash dividends of 2.5 cents per share to stockholders on a quarterly basis through November of 2013. In February 2014, we increased the quarterly cash dividend to 5 cents per share and paid quarterly cash dividends at this level through the fourth quarter 2014. Beginning in February 2015, we increased the quarterly cash dividend to 10 cents per share and paid quarterly</font><font style="display: inline;"> cash dividends at this level through the fourth quarter 2015. Beginning in February 2016, we increased the quarterly cash dividend to 11.5 cents per share and paid quarterly cash dividends through the fourth quarter 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On February 7, 2017 the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend </font><font style="display: inline;">of 12.5 cents</font><font style="display: inline;"> per share, payable on February 28, 2017 to stockholders of record on February 21, 2017.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our ability to pay dividends is subject to the restrictions of the Delaware General Corporation Law. Because we are a bank holding company with no significant assets other than our bank subsidiary, we currently depend upon dividends from our bank subsidiary for the majority of our revenues. </font><font style="display: inline;">Various banking laws applicable to the Bank limit the payment of dividends, management fees and other distributions by the Bank to the holding company, and may therefore limit our ability to pay dividends on our common stock.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the terms of each of our two outstanding trust preferred financings, including our related subordinated debentures, which occurred on June 30, 2003 and April 8, 2004, respectively, we cannot declare or pay any dividends or distributions (other than stock dividends) on, or redeem, purchase, acquire or make a liquidation payment with respect to, any shares of our capital stock if (1) an event of default under any of the subordinated debenture agreements has occurred and is continuing, or (2) we defer payment of interest on the TruPS for a period of up to 60 consecutive months as long as we are in compliance with all covenants of the agreement. At December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, interest payments on our two trust preferred financings were current.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Any future determination relating to dividend policy will be made at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend on a number of factors, including general business conditions, our financial results, our future business prospects, capital requirements, contractual, legal and regulatory restrictions on the payment of dividends by us to our stockholders or by the Bank to the holding company, and such other factors as our Board of Directors may deem relevant</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Contractual Obligations and Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Bank is a party to credit-related financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk entered into in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of the Bank&#x2019;s customers. These financial instruments include commitments</font><font style="display: inline;"> to extend credit, standby letters of credit and commercial letters of credit. Such commitments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk in excess of the amount recognized in the consolidated balance sheets. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Our exposure to credit loss is represented by the contractual amount of these commitments. We follow the same credit policies in making commitments as </font><font style="display: inline;">we do</font><font style="display: inline;"> for on-balance sheet instruments.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<a name="Item7A"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 7</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">A</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Market risk is the risk of loss in a financial instrument arising from adverse changes in market prices and rates, foreign currency exchange rates, commodity prices and equity prices. Our market risk arises primarily from interest rate risk inherent in our lending</font><font style="display: inline;">, investing a</font><font style="display: inline;">nd deposit taking activities.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">To that end, management actively monitors and manages our interest rate risk exposure.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">We have not entered into any market risk sensitive instruments for trading purposes.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">We manage our interest rate sensitivity by matching the repricing opportunities on our earning assets to those on our funding liabilities.</font><font style="display: inline;"> In order </font><font style="display: inline;">to manage the repricing characteristics of our assets and liabilities</font><font style="display: inline;">, we use various strategies</font><font style="display: inline;"> designed to ensure that </font><font style="display: inline;">our </font><font style="display: inline;">exposure to interest rate fluctuations is limited </font><font style="display: inline;">in accordance with </font><font style="display: inline;">our guidelines of acceptable levels of risk-taking.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Balance sheet hedging strategies, including </font><font style="display: inline;">monitoring </font><font style="display: inline;">the terms and pricing of loans and deposits and managing the deployment of our securities, are used to reduce</font><font style="display: inline;"> mismatches in interest rate re</font><font style="display: inline;">pricing </font><font style="display: inline;">between our </font><font style="display: inline;">portfolio </font><font style="display: inline;">of </font><font style="display: inline;">assets and their funding sources. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Credit Risk-Related Contingent </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Features</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company enters</font><font style="display: inline;"> into interest rate swap contracts with certain commercial banking customers to facilitate the customer&#x2019;s respective risk management strategies</font><font style="display: inline;"> and for the purpose of securing long-term borrowing rates</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Customer</font><font style="display: inline;"> interest rate swaps are simultaneously hedged by offsetting interest rate swaps that the Company executes with a third party, such that the Company minimizes its net risk exposure resulting from such transactions.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Thus, these existing interest rate derivatives result from a service provided to certain qualifying customers and, therefore, are not used to manage interest rate risk in the Company&#x2019;s assets or liabilities.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has entered into interest rate swap contracts to mitigate interest rate risk attributed to its current mix of assets and liabilities. These interest rate swaps are accounted for as cash flow hedges and are marked to market through Other Comprehensive Income (&#x201C;OCI&#x201D;). The fluctuations in market value related to these interest rate swaps are generally in the opposite direction of fluctuations in market value related to our available for sale investment portfolio allowing us to mitigate the impact of market value fluctuations on OCI.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Management</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> evaluates </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> credit risk associated with its interest rate swaps by evaluating the maximum potential credit exposure prior to the execution of the interest rate swap.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">This maximum potential credit exposure is evaluated by executive management in relation to the Company&#x2019;s Derivatives and Hedging Policy.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">On a quarterly basis, the actual credit risk for all swaps is reported to the Company&#x2019;s asset-liability management committee and compared to the maximum exposure approved in the Company&#x2019;s Derivatives and Hedging Policy. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company has agreements with its derivative counterparties that contain a provision where if the Company defaults on any of its indebtedness, including&nbsp;default where repayment&nbsp;of the indebtedness has not been accelerated by the lender,&nbsp;then the Company could also be declared in default on its derivative obligations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company also has agreements with certain of its derivative counterparties that contain a provision where if the Company fails to maintain its status as a well-capitalized institution, then the counterparty could terminate the derivative positions and the Company would be required to settle its obligations under the agreements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">As of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, the fair value </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of derivatives in a net liability position, which excludes any adjustment for nonperformance risk related to these agreements, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">was $1.9 million.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> The Company</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> has minimum collateral posting thresholds with certain of its derivative counterparties, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">had </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">posted $4.2 million in collateral as of December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2016 in relation to these thresholds. If the Company had breached any of these provisions</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> at December</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">31,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, it would have been required to settle its obligations under the agreements at the termination value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Net Interest Income Modeling</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our Asset Liability Management Committee, or ALCO, oversees our exposure to and mitigation of interest rate risk and, along with our Board of Directors, reviews our exposure to interest rate risk at least quarterly. The committee is composed of members of our senior management. The ALCO monitors interest rate risk by analyzing the potential impact on the net portfolio value and net interest income from potential changes in interest rates, and considers the impact of alternative strategies or changes in balance sheet structure. The ALCO manages our balance sheet in part to minimize the potential impact of changes in interest rates on net portfolio value and net interest income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">72</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#TableofContents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Interest rate risk exposure is measured using interest rate sensitivity analysis to evaluate fluctuations in net portfolio value and net interest income in the event of hypothetical changes in interest rates. If potential changes to net portfolio value and net interest income from hypothetical interest rate changes are not within the limits approved by the Board of Directors, the Board may direct management to adjust the Bank&#x2019;s mix of assets and liabilities to bring interest rate risk within these limits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We monitor and evaluate our interest rate risk position on at least a quarterly basis using net interest income simulation analysis under 100, 200 and 300 basis point change scenarios (see below). Each of these analyses measures different interest rate risk factors inherent in the financial statements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our primary interest rate risk measurement tool, the &#x201C;Net Interest Income Simulation Analysis&#x201D;, measures interest rate risk and the effect of hypothetical interest rate changes on net interest income. This analysis incorporates all of our assets and liabilities together with forecasted changes in the balance sheet and assumptions that reflect the current interest rate environment. Through these simulations, we estimate the impact on net interest income of an immediate change in market rates of 100, 200 and 300 basis points upward or downward, over a one year period. Assumptions are made to project rates for new loans and deposits based on historical analysis, our outlook and repricing strategies. Asset prepayments and other market risks are developed from industry estimates of prepayment speeds and other market changes. Since the results of these simulations can be significantly influenced by the assumptions on which the simulations rely, we also evaluate the sensitivity of simulation results to changes in underlying assumptions</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">The following table shows the projected net interest income increase or decrease over the next 12 months as of December</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">31,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">December 31, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">201</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2016, we </font><font style="display: inline;">had </font><font style="display: inline;">moved toward a more asset sensitive balance sheet as compared to December 31, 2015 primarily due to variable rate loans acquired in the Home State transaction and a lower overnight funding position. At December 31, 2016, we are positioned to have a short-term favorable interest income impact in the event of an immediate 300, 200 or 100 basis point increase in market interest rates. Our asset sensitivity is mostly due to the amount of variable rate loans on the books and is partially mitigated by interest rate floors, or minimum rates: as rates rise, the loan rate may continue to be at the minimum rate. We also anticipate that deposit rates, other than time deposit rates, would increase immediately in a rising rate environment, but at a reduced magnitude. </font><font style="display: inline;">In our market risk table above, we model that interest rates on our NOW and savings accounts will increase </font><font style="display: inline;">11</font><font style="display: inline;"> percent of any increase in market interest rates For interest-bearing demand and money market accounts, we model that interest rates would increase 65 percent of any increase in market interest rates. </font><font style="display: inline;">Additionally, the interest rates paid on our FHLB line of credit advances would increase immediately as well. In addition to performing net interest income modeling, we also monitor the impact an instantaneous change in interest rates would have on our economic value of equity. We anticipate a reduction in the economic value of equity in a rising rate environment as the reduction in the value of our fixed rate earning assets would outweigh the corresponding increase in value of our low cost deposits.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We estimate that our net interest income would decline in a 100, 200 or 300 basis point falling rate environment. This is consistent with our belief that our balance sheet is asset sensitive. At December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2016, it is not possible for the majority of our deposit rates to fall 100 to 300 basis points since most deposit rates were already </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">73</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#TableofContents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">below 100 basis points. At December 31, 2016, the loss of gross interest income in a falling interest rate environment is expected to exceed the corresponding reduction in interest expense in a falling rate environment. We believe that this scenario is </font><font style="display: inline;">currently </font><font style="display: inline;">very unlikely. The target federal funds rate is currently set by the Federal Open Market Committee of the Federal Reserve Board at a rate of between 50 and 75 basis points and the prime rate has historically been set at a rate of 300 basis points over the target federal funds rate. Our interest rate risk modeling assumes that the prime rate would continue to be set at a rate of 300 basis points over the target federal funds rate; therefore, a 200 basis point decline in overall rates would only result in a </font><font style="display: inline;">50</font><font style="display: inline;"> to</font><font style="display: inline;"> 75</font><font style="display: inline;"> basis point decline in both target federal funds rate and the prime rate. Further, other rates that are currently below 1% or 2% (e.g.&nbsp;short-term U.S. Treasuries and LIBOR) are modeled to not fall below 0% with an overall 100 or 200 basis point decrease in rates. Many of our variable rate loans are set to an index tied to the prime rate, the target federal funds rate or LIBOR, therefore, a further decrease in rates would likely not have a substantial impact on loan yields.</font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 9pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;background-color:yellow;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<a name="ManagementReport"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">The management of Guaranty Bancorp, including its consolidated subsidiary, is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. The Company&#x2019;s internal control system was designed to provide reasonable assurance to the Company&#x2019;s management and Board of Directors regarding the preparation and fair presentation of published financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations. Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation and presentation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Management maintains a comprehensive system of controls intended to ensure that transactions are executed in accordance with management&#x2019;s authorization, assets are safeguarded, and financial records are reliable. Management also takes steps to see that information and communication flows are effective and to monitor performance, including performance of internal control procedures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">As of December 31, 2016, Guaranty Bancorp management assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting based on the framework established in </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Internal Control-Integrated Framework </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">issu</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">ed by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission &#x2013; 2013 (COSO). Based on this assessment, management has determined that the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2016 was effective.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements should they occur. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree or compliance with the control procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">As permitted, the Company has excluded the operations of Home State Bancorp acquired during 2016, which is described in Note 3 of the consolidated financial statements, from the scope of this report.&nbsp; The assets acquired in this acquisition and excluded from management's assessment on internal control over financial reporting comprised approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">28</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">% of total consolidated assets as of December 31, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Crowe Horwath LLP, the independent registered public accounting firm that audited the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2016 and 2015, included in the Annual Report on Form 10-K filed February 28, 2017, has issued an audit report on the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2016. The report, which expresses an unqualified opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2016, is included in this Item under the heading &#x201C;Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm.&#x201D; </font>
		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3pt 50.4pt;text-indent: -50.4pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 9pt"><a name="AuditReport"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3pt 50.4pt;text-indent: -50.4pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 8pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:8pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Board of Directors and Stockholders</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Guaranty Bancorp</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Denver, Colorado</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Guaranty Bancorp and Subsidiaries (&#x201C;the Company&#x201D;) as of December 31, 2016 and 2015, and the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, changes in stockholders' equity, and cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December 31, 2016. We also have audited the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2016, based on criteria established in the </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> (2013), issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). The Company&#x2019;s management is responsible for these consolidated financial statements, for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial statements and an opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement and whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audits of the consolidated financial statements included examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. Our audits also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;background-color:yellow;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of consolidated financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company's internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of consolidated financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">As permitted, the Company has excluded the operations of Home State Bancorp acquired during 2016, which is described in Note 3 of the consolidated financial statements, from the scope of management&#x2019;s report on internal control over financial reporting. As such, it has also been excluded from the scope of our audit of internal control over financial reporting.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of Guaranty Bancorp as of December 31, 2016 and 2015, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December 31, 2016 in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Also in our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2016, based on criteria established in the </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> (2013), issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Organization </font>

References to &#x201C;Guaranty Bancorp&#x201D; or to the &#x201C;holding company&#x201D; refer to the parent company on a stand-alone basis.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Bank is a full-</font><font style="display: inline;">service community bank offering an array of banking products and services to the communities it serves along the Front Range of Colorado including accepting time and demand deposits and originating commercial loans, commercial and residential real estate loans, Small Business Administration (&#x201C;SBA&#x201D;) guaranteed loans and consumer loans. The Bank together with its wholly owned subsidiaries, Private Capital Management, LLC (&#x201C;PCM&#x201D;) and Cherry Hills Investment Advisors, Inc. (&#x201C;CHIA&#x201D;), provide wealth management services, including private banking, investment management and trust services. Substantially all of the Bank&#x2019;s loans are secured by specific items of collateral, including business assets, commercial and residential real estate, which include land or improved land and consumer assets. Commercial loans are expected to be repaid from cash flow from the operations of businesses that have taken out the loans. There are no significant concentrations of loans to any one industry or customer.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">On September 8, 2016, the Company completed the acquisition of Home State Bancorp (&#x201C;Home State&#x201D;), based in Loveland, Colorado, in exchange for a combination of Company stock and cash. T</font><font style="display: inline;">he transaction </font><font style="display: inline;">enhanced the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">balance sheet </font><font style="display: inline;">liquidity </font><font style="display: inline;">and supports the Company&#x2019;s objective of serving the banking needs of northern Colorado business and consumer customers. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The accounting and reporting policies of the Company conform to generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America. All material intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolida</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">tion. The Company&#x2019;s financial statements reflect all adjustments that are, in the opinion of management, necessary for a fair presentation of its financial position and results of operations for the periods presented. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(b)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 15pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Business Combinations </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 48.95pt;text-indent: -24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for acquisitions of businesses using the acquisition method of accounting. Under the acquisition method, assets acquired and liabilities assumed are recorded at their estimated fair value upon the date of acquisition. Management utilizes various valuation techniques including discounted cash flow analyses to determine the fair values of assets acquired and liabilities assumed. Any excess of purchase price over amounts allocated to the acquired assets, including identifiable intangible assets, and liabilities assumed is recorded as goodwill. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">The preparation of the consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities as of the dates of the consolidated balance sheets and income and expense for the periods presented. Actual results could differ significantly from those estimates. </font>
