		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">e</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Time Deposits with Banks</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company may invest in short term, fully insured time deposits with other banks</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">f</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Securities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.5pt;text-indent: -27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">S</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ecurities are classified as held to maturity and carried at amortized cost when management has the positive intent and ability to hold them to maturity. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">S</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ecurities not classified as held to maturity are classified as available for sale. Securities available for sale are carried at fair value, with unrealized gains and losses reported in other comprehensive income, net of tax.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Interest income includes amortization of purchase premium or discount. Premiums and discounts on securities are amortized </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">according to</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> the effective </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">interest</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> method without anticipating prepayments, except for mortgage-backed securities where prepayments are anticipated. Gains and losses on sales are recorded on the trade date and determined using the specific identification method.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Management evaluates securities for other-than-temporary impairment (&#x201C;OTTI&#x201D;) on a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic or market conditions warrant such an evaluation. For securities in an unrealized loss position, management considers the extent and duration of the unrealized loss and the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer. Management also assesses whether it intends to sell, or it is more likely than not that it will be required to sell, a security in an unrealized loss position before recovery of its amortized cost basis. If either of the criteria regarding intent or requirement to sell is met, the entire difference between amortized cost and fair value is recognized as an impairment t</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">o</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> earnings. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The investments in bank stocks are reviewed by management quarterly for potential OTTI. This quarterly review considers the credit quality of the institution, the institution&#x2019;s ability to repurchase shares and the Company&#x2019;s carrying value in the shares relativ</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">e to</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> book value. Based on these reviews, management concluded that there was </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">no</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> impairment during 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 48.95pt;text-indent: -24.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.7pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">g</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Loans and Loan Commitments </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 46.8pt;text-indent: -24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company ex</font><font style="display: inline;">tends commercial, real estate</font><font style="display: inline;"> and consumer loans to customers. A substantial portion of the loan portfolio consists of commercial and real estate loans throughout the Front Range of Colorado. The ability of the Company&#x2019;s borrowers to honor their contracts is generally dependent upon the real estate and general economic conditions prevailing in Colorado, among other factors. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Purchased loans for which there was no evidence of credit deterioration upon acquisition and for which collection of all contractually required payments upon acquisition was considered probable are referred to collectively as non-purchased credit impaired loans, or &#x201C;Non-PCI&#x201D; loans. Purchased loans for which there was at the acquisition date evidence of credit deterioration since origination and for which collection of all contractually required payments was not probable were designated as and referred to as purchased credit impaired or &#x201C;PCI&#x201D; loans. In the September 8, 2016 Home State transaction, the Company designated </font><font style="display: inline;">$2,108,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> of loans as PCI. As of December 31, 2016 </font><font style="display: inline;">$1,902,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> in PCI loans remained in the Company&#x2019;s loan portfolio. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Loans that management has the intent and ability to hold for the foreseeable future or until maturity or payoff are reported at their outstanding unpaid principal balances, adjusted for charge-offs, the allowance for loan losses and any deferred fees or costs. </font><font style="display: inline;">Acquired loans are recorded upon acquisition at fair value, with no associated allowance for loan loss. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">However, if subsequent to acquisition the credit quality of an acquired loan deteriorates, an allowance may be required. </font><font style="display: inline;">Accounting for loans is performed consistently across all portfolio segments and classes. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A portfolio segment is defined in accounting guidance as the level at which an entity develops and documents a systematic methodology to determine its allowance for loan losses. A class is defined in accounting guidance as a group of loans having similar initial measurement attributes, risk characteristics and methods for monitoring and assessing risk. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Interest income is accrued on the unpaid principal balance of the Company&#x2019;s loans. Loan origination fees, net of direct origination costs, are deferred and recognized as an adjustment to the related loan yield </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">84</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">GUARANTY BANCORP AND SUBSIDIARIES</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#TableofContents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">using the effective interest method without anticipating prepayments. Purchase discount or premium on acquired, Non-PCI loans is recognized as an adjustment to interest income over the contractual life of such loans using the effective interest method, or taken into income when the related loans are paid off or sold. With respect to PCI loans, the &#x201C;accretable yield&#x201D;, calculated as the excess of undiscounted expected cash flows over the present value of expected cash flows, is accreted into income over the term of the loan assuming the amount and timing of cash flows are reasonably estimable. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The accrual of interest on loans is discontinued (and the loan is put on nonaccrual status) at the time the loan is 90 days past due unless the loan is well secured and in process of collection. The time at which a loan enters past due status is based on the contractual terms of the loan. In all cases, loans are placed on nonaccrual or charged-off prior to the date on </font><font style="display: inline;">which they would otherwise enter past due status if collection of principal or interest is considered doubtful. The interest on a nonaccrual loan is accounted for using the cost-recovery or cash-basis method, until the loan qualifies for a return to the accrual-basis method. Under the cost-recovery method, interest income is not recognized until the loan balance is reduced to zero, with payments received being applied first to the principal balance of the loan. Under the cash-basis method, interest income is recognized when the payment is received in cash.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">A loan is returned to accrual status after the delinquent borrower&#x2019;s financial condition has improved, when all the principal and interest amounts contractually due are brought current and when the likelihood of the borrower making future timely payments </font><font style="display: inline;">is</font><font style="display: inline;"> reasonably assured.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Financial</font><font style="display: inline;"> instruments include off</font><font style="display: inline;">&#8209;balance sheet credit instruments, such as commitments to make loans and commercial letters of credit issued to meet customer financing needs. The face amount of each item represents the Company&#x2019;s total exposure to loss with respect to the item before considering customer collateral or ability to repay. Such financial instruments are recorded when they are funded</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.7pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">h</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Allowance for Loan Losses and Allowance for Unfunded Commitments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49pt;text-indent: -24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The allowance for loan losses or &#x201C;the allowance&#x201D; is a valuation allowance for probable incurred loan losses and is reported as a reduction of outstanding loan balances.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management evaluates the amount of the allowance on a regular basis based upon its periodic review of the collectability of the Company&#x2019;s loans. Factors affecting the collectability of the loans include historical </font><font style="display: inline;">loss </font><font style="display: inline;">experience, the nature and volume of the loan portfolio, adverse situations that may affect </font><font style="display: inline;">the </font><font style="display: inline;">borrowers&#x2019; ability to repay, </font><font style="display: inline;">the </font><font style="display: inline;">estimated value of any underlying collateral and prevailing economic conditions. This evaluation is inherently subjective as it requires estimates that are susceptible to significant revision as more information becomes available. Management maintains the allowance at a level that it deems appropriate to adequately provide for </font><font style="display: inline;">probable incurred losses</font><font style="display: inline;"> in the loan portfolio and other extensions of credit. The Company&#x2019;s methodology for estimating the allowance is consistent across all portfolio segments and classes of loans. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Loans deemed </font><font style="display: inline;">to be uncollectible are charged-</font><font style="display: inline;">off and deducted from the allowance. The Company&#x2019;s loan portfolio primarily consists of non-homogeneous commercial and real estate loans where charge-offs are considered on a loan-by-loan basis based on the facts and circumstances, including management&#x2019;s evaluation of collateral values in comparison to book values on collateral-dependent loans. Charge-offs on smaller balance unsecured homogenous type loans such as overdrafts and ready reserves are recognized by the time the loan in question is </font><font style="display: inline;">90</font><font style="display: inline;"> days past due. The provision for loan losses and recoveries on loans previously charged-off are added to the allowance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The allowance consists of both specific and general components. The specific component relates to loans that are individually classified as impaired. All loans are subject to individual impairment evaluation should the </font><font style="display: inline;">pertinent </font><font style="display: inline;">facts and circumstances suggest that such evaluation is necessary. Factors considered by management in determining impairment include the loan&#x2019;s payment status and the probability of collecting scheduled principal and interest payments when they become due. Loans that experience insignificant payment delays and payment shortfalls generally are not classified as impaired. A loan is considered impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Company will be unable to collect the scheduled payments of principal or interest when due according to the contractual terms of the original underlying loan agreement. Management determines the significance of payment delays and payment shortfalls on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration all of the circumstances surrounding the loan and the borrower, including the length of the delay, the reasons for the delay, the borrower&#x2019;s prior payment record, and the amount of the shortfall in relation to the principal and interest owed. If a loan is impaired, a portion, if </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">85</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">GUARANTY BANCORP AND SUBSIDIARIES</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#TableofContents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">any, of the allowance is allocated so that the loan is reported at the present value of estimated future cash flows using the loan&#x2019;s original contractual rate or at the fair value of collateral</font><font style="display: inline;">, less estimated selling costs,</font><font style="display: inline;"> if repayment is expected solely from collateral. </font><font style="display: inline;">Troubled debt restructurings (&#x201C;TDRs&#x201D;) are separately identified for impairment disclosures. If a TDR is considered to be a collateral-dependent loan, </font><font style="display: inline;">impairment of the loan is measured using the</font><font style="display: inline;"> fair value of the collateral, less estimated selling costs. Likewise, if a TDR is not collateral-dependent, impairment is measured by the present value of estimated future cash flows using the loan&#x2019;s effective rate at inception. For TDRs that subsequently default, the Company determines the amount of reserve in accordance with its accounting policy for the allowance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The general component of the allowance covers all other loans not specifically identified as impaired and is determined by calculating losses recognized by portfolio segment during the current credit cycle and adjusted </font><font style="display: inline;">based on management&#x2019;s evaluation of various qualitative factors</font><font style="display: inline;">. In performing this calculation, loans are aggregated into one of </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> portfolio segments: Real Estate, Consumer and Co</font><font style="display: inline;">mmercial &amp; Other. An assessment</font><font style="display: inline;"> of risks impacting loans in each of these portfolio segments is performed</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and qualitative adjustment factors, which will adjust the historical loss rate</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> are estimated. These qualitative adjustment factors consider current conditions relative to conditions present throughout the current credit cycle in the </font><font style="display: inline;">following areas:</font><font style="display: inline;"> credit quality, loan class concentration levels, economic conditions, loan growth dynamics and organizational conditions. The histo</font><font style="display: inline;">r</font><font style="display: inline;">ical loss experience is adjusted for management&#x2019;s estimate of the impact of these factors based on the risks present for each portfolio segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes a liability in relation to unfunded commitments that is intended to represent the</font><font style="display: inline;"> estimated future losses on </font><font style="display: inline;">commitments. In calculating the amount of this liability, management considers the amount of </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> off-balance sheet commitments, estimated utilization factors and loan specific risk factors. The Company&#x2019;s liability for unfunded commitments is calculated </font><font style="display: inline;">quarterly and the liability is </font><font style="display: inline;">included under &#x201C;other liabilities&#x201D; in the consolidated balance sheet.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(i)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 13pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Loans Held for Sale</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.5pt;text-indent: -27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">P</font><font style="display: inline;">articular loans may be considered &#x201C;held</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">for</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">sale&#x201D; as of the Company&#x2019;s balance sheet date. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company routinely sells SBA guaranteed loans, and h</font><font style="display: inline;">istorically </font><font style="display: inline;">has </font><font style="display: inline;">designated select classified or nonaccrual loans as held-for-sale as part of its strategy to dispose of these non-earning assets.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Once the decision is made to sell a loan</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> the loan </font><font style="display: inline;">is designated as held </font><font style="display: inline;">for</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">sale and carried at the lower of cost or fair value, with any required write-down being taken at the time of the reclassification. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:22pt;"><p style="width:22pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;;"> (j)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Transfers of Financial Assets</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales when control over the assets has been relinquished. Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when the assets have been isolated from the Company, the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets, and the Company does not maintain effective control over the transferred assets through an agreement to repurchase them before their maturity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">(k)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 13pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Other Real Estate Owned and Foreclosed Assets</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Assets acquired through, or in lieu of, loan foreclosure are initially recorded at fair value less costs to sell when acquired, establishing a new cost basis. If the asset&#x2019;s fair value declines subsequent to the asset&#x2019;s acquisition, a valuation allowance is recorded through expense. Operating revenues and expenses of these assets and reductions in the fair value of the assets are included in noninterest expense. Gains and losses on their disposition are also included in noninterest expense.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">(l)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 13pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Premises and Equipment </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.5pt;text-indent: -27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Land is carried at cost. Buildings, equipment and software are carried at cost, less accumulated depreciation and amortization computed on the straight-line method over the useful life of the asset. Leasehold improvements are depreciated over the shorter of their estimated useful life or the lease term. Buildings and leasehold improvements carry an estimated useful life of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">five</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">40</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> years and equipment and software carry an estimated useful life of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">one</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">15</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> years. Repairs and maintenance are charged to noninterest expense as incurred. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Bank is a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) system. Members are required to own a certain amount of stock based on the level of borrowings and other factors, and may invest in additional amounts. The Bank also owns Federal Reserve Bank (FRB) stock, Bankers</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Bank of the West (BBW) stock and Pacific Coast Bankers&#x2019; Bank (PCBB) stock. FHLB, FRB, BBW and PCBB stock is carried at cost, classified as a restricted security, and periodically reviewed for impairment based on the likelihood of ultimate recovery of par value. Both cash and stock dividends are reported as income</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">n</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Other Intangible Assets</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.5pt;text-indent: -27pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:27.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill was recorded in the Home State transaction and represents the excess of the purchase price over the fair value of acquired tangible assets, identifiable intangible assets and liabilities. Goodwill is assessed at least annually for impairment and any such impairment is recognized in the period identified. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:27.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:27.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Intangible assets acquired in a business combination are amortized over their estimated useful lives to their estimated residual values and evaluated for impairment whenever changes in circumstances indicate that such an evaluation is necessary.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Core deposit intangible assets (&#x201C;CDI assets&#x201D;) are recognized at the time of their acquisition based on valuations prepared by independent third parties or other estimates of fair value. In preparing such valuations, management considers variables such as deposit servicing costs, attrition rates and market discount rates. CDI assets are amortized to expense over their useful lives, ranging from </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;"> years to </font><font style="display: inline;">15</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Customer relationship intangible assets are recognized at the time of their acquisition based upon management&#x2019;s estimate of their fair value. In preparing their valuation, management considers variables such as growth in existing customer base, attrition rates and market discount rates. The c</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ustomer relationship intangible assets are amortized to expense over their estimated useful life, which has been estimated to be </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">10</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> years. The Company has recognized </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">t</font><font style="display: inline;">hree</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> customer relationship intangible assets as a result of the acquisitions of PCM on July 31, 2012, CHIA on July 16, 2014 and Home State on September 8, 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.7pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.7pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">o</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Impairment</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"> of Long-Lived Assets </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.7pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Long-lived assets, such as premises and equipment, and finite-lived intangible assets subject to amortization, are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying value of an asset may not be recoverable. The recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying value of the asset to the estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to be generated by the asset. If the carrying value of an asset exceeds its estimated undiscounted future cash flows, an impairment charge is recognized by the amount by which the carrying value of the asset exceeds the fair value of the asset, less costs to sell. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Assets to be </font><font style="display: inline;">disposed of are reported at the lower of their carrying value or fair value less costs to sell, and are no longer depreciated. During 2016, the Company recognized </font><font style="display: inline;">an </font><font style="display: inline;">$185,000</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">impairment charge</font><font style="display: inline;"> on a </font><font style="display: inline;">long-lived asset; the asset was designated as </font><font style="display: inline;">held for sale and included in &#x201C;other assets&#x201D; in the December 31, 2016 consolidated balance sheet.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">During 2015 the Company recognized </font><font style="display: inline;">$122,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> in impairment charges on </font><font style="display: inline;">the sale of a former branch facility. An impairment charge of </font><font style="display: inline;">$186,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> on the same former branch facility was recognized in 2014. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">p</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Derivative Instruments </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company records all derivatives on</font><font style="display: inline;"> its consolidated balance sheet</font><font style="display: inline;"> at fair value. At the inception of a derivative contract, the Company designates the derivative as one of three types based on the Company&#x2019;s intentions and belief as to the derivative&#x2019;s likely effectiveness as a hedge. These three types are (1)</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">a hedge of the fair value of a recognized asset or liability or of an unrecognized firm commitment (&#x201C;fair value hedge&#x201D;),</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">(2)</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">a hedge of a forecasted transaction or the variability of cash flows to be received or paid related to a recognized asset or liability (&#x201C;cash flow hedge&#x201D;), or (3)</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">an instrument with no hedging designation (&#x201C;stand-alone derivative&#x201D;). To date, the Company has entered into cash flow hedges and stand-alone derivative agreements but has not entered into any fair value hedges. For a cash flow hedge, the gain or loss on the derivative is reported in other comprehensive income and is reclassified into earnings in the same periods </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">during which the hedged transaction </font><font style="display: inline;">impacts</font><font style="display: inline;"> earnings. Any portion of the cash flow hedge not deemed highly effective in hedging the changes in expected cash flows of the hedged item </font><font style="display: inline;">is</font><font style="display: inline;"> recognized immediately in current earnings. Changes in the fair value of derivatives that do not qualify for hedge accounting are reported currently in earnings, as noninterest income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company formally documents the relationship between derivatives and hedged items, as well as the risk-management objective and the strategy for undertaking hedge transactions, at the inception of the derivative contract. This documentation includes linking cash flow hedges to specific assets and liabilities on the balance sheet or to specific firm commitments or forecasted transactions. The Company also formally assesses, both at the hedge&#x2019;s inception and on an ongoing basis, whether the hedge is highly effective in offsetting changes in cash flows of the hedged items.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 16.8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">q</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Stock Incentive Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s Amended and Restated 2005 Stock Incentive Plan (the &#x201C;Incentive Plan&#x201D;) provided for the grant of equity-based awards representing up to a total of </font><font style="display: inline;">1,700,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of voting common stock to key employees, nonemployee directors, consultants and prospective employees. The Incentive Plan expired by its terms on April 4, 2015. At the Company&#x2019;s annual meeting of stockholders on May 5, 2015, the Company&#x2019;s stockholders approved the Guaranty Bancorp 2015 Long-Term Incentive Plan (the &#x201C;2015 Plan&#x201D;), which had been previously approved by the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors. The 2015 Plan provides for the grant of stock options, stock awards, stock unit awards, performance stock awards, stock appreciation rights, and other equity-based awards representing up to a total of </font><font style="display: inline;">935,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of voting common stock to key employees, nonemployee directors, consultants and prospective employees. All awards issued under the Incentive Plan will remain outstanding in accordance with their terms despite the expiration of the Incentive Plan; however, any awards granted subsequent to the expiration of the Incentive Plan have been, and will continue to be, issued under the 2015 Plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of </font><font style="display: inline;">December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2016, the Company had granted stock awards under both the Incentive Plan and the 2015 plan</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company recognizes stock compensation expense for services received in a share-based payment transaction over the requisite service period, generally defined as the vesting period. For awards with graded vesting, compensation cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period for the entire award. The compensation cost of employee and director services received in exchange for stock awards is based on the grant date fair value of the award, as determined by quoted market prices. Stock compensation expense is recognized using an estimated forfeiture rate, adjusted as necessary to reflect actual forfeitures. The Company has issued stock awards that vest based on the passage of time over service periods of </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;"> years (in some cases vesting in annual installments, in other cases cliff vesting at the end of the service period), and other stock awards that vest contingent upon the satisfaction of certain performance conditions. The last date on which outstanding performance stoc</font><font style="display: inline;">k awards may vest is February 14</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2019. At December 31, 2016, certain performance stock awards were expected to vest prior to their expiration. Should expectations of future financial performance change, expense to be recognized in future periods could</font><font style="display: inline;"> be impacted.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:26.45pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">r</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Stock Repurchase Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">t</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 25.95pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Income tax expense is the total of the current year&#x2019;s income tax payable or refundable and the increase or decrease in deferred tax assets and liabilities. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and</font><font style="display: inline;"> their respective tax bases and operating loss and tax credit carry forwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period of the enactment date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when, in the opinion of management, it is more likely than not that </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company will not realize </font><font style="display: inline;">some portion</font><font style="display: inline;"> of</font><font style="display: inline;">, or the entire deferred tax</font><font style="display: inline;"> asset</font><font style="display: inline;">. In assessing the Company&#x2019;s likelihood of realizing deferred tax assets, management evaluates both positive and negative evidence, including the existence of any cumulative losses in the current year and the prior two years, the amount of taxes paid in available carry-back years, forecasts of future income, taking into account applicable tax planning strategies, and assessments of current and future economic and business conditions. Management performs this analysis quarterly and adjusts as necessary. At December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> and December</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company had a net deferred tax </font><font style="display: inline;">asset of $</font><font style="display: inline;">4,846,000 </font><font style="display: inline;">and</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;$</font><font style="display: inline;">7,912,000</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> respectively, </font><font style="display: inline;">which includes the </font><font style="display: inline;">deferred tax asset associated with the net unrealized gain (loss) on securities</font><font style="display: inline;">. After analyzing the composition of and changes in the deferred tax assets and liabilities and considering the Company&#x2019;s forecasted future taxable income and various tax planning strategies, including the intent to hold the securities available for sale that were in a loss position until maturity, management determined that as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> it </font><font style="display: inline;">was</font><font style="display: inline;"> more likely than not that the net deferred tax asset </font><font style="display: inline;">would</font><font style="display: inline;"> be fully realized. </font><font style="display: inline;">As </font><font style="display: inline;">a result, there was </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> valuation allowance with respect to the Company&#x2019;s deferred tax asset as of December</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">31,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> or December</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company and the Bank are sub</font><font style="display: inline;">ject to U.S. federal income tax, State of Colorado income tax and income tax in other states.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Generally, t</font><font style="display: inline;">he Company is no longer subje</font><font style="display: inline;">ct to examination by Federal </font><font style="display: inline;">taxing authorities for years before </font><font style="display: inline;">2013 and is no longer subject to examination by the State </font><font style="display: inline;">of Colorado </font><font style="display: inline;">for years before 2012. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Company recognizes interest related to income tax matters as interest expense and penalties related to income tax </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">matters as other noninterest expense. At </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">December 31, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, the Company did not have any amounts accrued </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">interest or penalties. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">u</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Segments of an Enterprise and</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"> Related Information</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.5pt;text-indent: -27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company operates as a single segment. The operating information used by the Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Chief Executive O</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">fficer for purposes of assessing performance and making operating decisions </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">impacting</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> the Company is the consolidated financial data presented in this report. For the years ended 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, the Company had one active operating subsidiary, Guaranty Bank and Trust Company. The Company has determined that banking is its </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">one</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> reportable business segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(v)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 13pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Earnings p</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">er Common Share</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.65pt;text-indent: -27.35pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.35pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Basic earnings per common share represents the earnings allocable to common stockholders divided by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Dilutive common shares that may be issued by the Company represent unvested stock awards subject to a service or performance condition.</font>
		</p>
