		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">On </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">February 7, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> the Company announced that its Board of Directors declared a quarterly </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">cash</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">dividend of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">12.5</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> cents per share, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">payable on </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">February 28, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to stockholders of record on </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">February&nbsp;21,&nbsp;2017</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(x</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Fair Values of Financial Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.5pt;text-indent: -27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Fair values of financial instruments are estimated using relevant market information and other assumptions, as</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> more fully disclosed in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8 &#x201C;Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. Fair value estimates involve uncertainties and matters of significant judgment regarding interest rates, credit risk, prepayments, and other factors, especially in the absence of broad markets for particular items. Changes in assumptions or in market conditions could significantly affect the estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">y</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Loss Contingencies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.5pt;text-indent: -27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Loss contingencies, including claims and legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business, are recorded as liabilities when the likelihood of a loss is probable and an amount or range of loss can be reasonably estimated. Loss contingencies are more fully </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">disclosed in Note 15 &#x201C;Legal Contingencies</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">z</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Recently Issued Accounting </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Standards </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 28.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Adoption of New Accounting Standards:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In April 2015, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (the &#x201C;FASB&#x201D;) issued accounting standards update 2015-03 modifying the presentation of debt issuance costs. The update requires that debt issuance costs be presented as a direct reduction of debt balances on the balance sheet. For public business entities, the amendments of this update are effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2015. </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">90</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">GUARANTY BANCORP AND SUBSIDIARIES</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#TableofContents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">As a result of this update the Company has presented debt issuance costs as a reduction of the related debt balance on the Company&#x2019;s balance sheet. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In September 2015, the FASB issued accounting standards update 2015-16 Simplifying the Accounting for Measurement-Period Adjustments. The update requires acquirers to adjust provisional amounts identified during the measurement period in the reporting period in which the adjustments are determined, rather than retrospectively adjusting previously reported information. Additional disclosure of the impact of measurement period adjustments on current year earnings will also be required. For public business entities, the amendments of this update are effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2015. This update did not have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In March 2016, the FASB issued accounting standards update 2016-09 Compensation-Stock Compensation. The purpose of the update was to simplify the accounting for share-based payment transactions, including the income tax consequences of such transactions. Under the provisions of the update the income tax consequences of excess tax benefits and deficiencies should be recognized in income tax expense in the reporting period in which the awards vest. Currently, excess tax benefits or deficiencies impact stockholders&#x2019; equity directly to the extent there is a cumulative excess tax benefit. In the event that a tax deficiency has occurred during the reporting period and a cumulative excess tax benefit does not exist, the tax deficiency is recognized in income tax expense under current GAAP. The update also provides that entities may continue to estimate forfeitures in accounting for stock based compensation or recognize them as they occur. The provisions of this update become effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2016, however early adoption was permitted beginning in 2016. The Company adopted the provisions of the update in the fourth quarter of 2016 with the most significant impact being </font><font style="display: inline;">$528,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> of excess tax benefit in restricted stock vestings directly benefiting 2016 income tax expense. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:27.9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Recently Issu</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">ed but not yet Effective Accounting Standards:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:27.9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the FASB issued accounting standards update 2014-09 Revenue from Contracts with Customers. The main provisions of the update require the identification of performance obligations within a contract and require the recognition of revenue based on a stand-alone allocation of contract revenue to each performance obligation. Performance obligations may be satisfied and revenue recognized over a period of time if: (i) the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits provided by the entity&#x2019;s performance as the entity performs, or (ii) the entity&#x2019;s performance creates or enhances an asset that the customer controls as the asset is created or enhanced, or (iii) the entity&#x2019;s performance does not create an asset with an alternative use to the entity and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date. The amendments of the update are to be effective for public entities beginning with interim and annual reporting periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2017. Management does not expect the requirements of this update to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:27.9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In January 2016, the FASB released accounting standards update 2016-01 Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Liabilities. The main provisions of the update are to eliminate the available for sale classification of accounting for equity securities and to adjust the fair value disclosures for financial instruments carried at amortized costs such that the disclosed fair values represent an exit price as opposed to an entry price. The provisions of this update will require that equity securities be carried at fair market value on the balance sheet and any periodic changes in value will be adjustments to the income statement. A practical expedient is provided for equity securities without a readily determinable fair value, such that these securities can be carried at cost less any impairment. The provisions of this update become effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2017. Management does not expect the requirements of this update to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In February 2016, the FASB issued accounting standards update 2016-02 Leases. The update requires all leases, with the exception of short-term leases that have contractual terms of no greater than one year, to be recorded on the balance sheet. Under the provisions of the update, leases classified as operating will be reflected on the balance sheet with the recognition of both a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. Under the update, a distinction will exist between finance and operating type leases and the rules for determining which classification a lease will fall into are similar to existing rules. For public business entities, the amendments of </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">91</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">GUARANTY BANCORP AND SUBSIDIARIES</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#TableofContents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">this update are effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2018. The update requires a modified retrospective transition under which comparative balance sheets from the earliest historical period presented will be revised to reflect what the financials would have looked like were the provisions of the update applied consistently in all prior periods. Management is in the process of evaluating the impacts of the update on the Company&#x2019;s financial position and does not expect the requirements of the update to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows. </font><font style="display: inline;">Based on leases outstanding at December 31, 2016, we anticipate </font><font style="display: inline;">total </font><font style="display: inline;">assets and </font><font style="display: inline;">total </font><font style="display: inline;">liabilities</font><font style="display: inline;"> will increase between </font><font style="display: inline;">$8,200,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">$9,800,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> as the result of additional leases being recognized on our balance sheet</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Decisions to repurchase, modify, or renew leases prior to the implementation date will impact the results of the Company&#x2019;s final analysis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In June 2016, the FASB issued accounting standards update 2016-13 Financial Instruments - Credit Losses, commonly referred to as &#x201C;CECL&#x201D;. The provisions of the update eliminate the probable initial recognition threshold under current GAAP which requires reserves to be based on an incurred loss methodology. Under CECL reserves required for financial assets measured at amortized cost will reflect an organization&#x2019;s estimate of all expected credit losses over the contractual term of the financial asset and thereby require the use of reasonable and supportable forecasts to estimate future credit losses. Because CECL encompasses all financial assets carried at amortized cost, the requirement that reserves be established based on an organization&#x2019;s reasonable and supportable estimate of expected credit losses extends to held to maturity (&#x201C;HTM&#x201D;) debt securities. Under the provisions of the update credit losses recognized on available for sale (&#x201C;AFS&#x201D;) debt securities will be presented as an allowance as opposed to a write-down. In addition, CECL will modify the accounting for purchased loans, with credit deterioration since origination, so that reserves are established at the date of acquisition for purchased loans. Under current GAAP a purchased loan&#x2019;s contractual balance is adjusted to fair value through a credit discount and no reserve is recorded on the purchased loan upon acquisition. Since under CECL reserves will be established for purchased loans at the time of acquisition the accounting for purchased loans is made more comparable to the accounting for originated loans. Finally, increased disclosure requirements under CECL require organizations to present the currently required credit quality disclosures disaggregated by the year of origination or vintage. The FASB expects that the evaluation of underwriting standards and credit quality trends by financial statement users will be enhanced with the additional vintage disclosures. For public business entities that are SEC filers the amendments of the update will become effective beginning January 1, 2020. The Company has formed a cross-functional committee </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">that is assessing our data and system needs. Management expects to recognize a one-time cumulative effect adjustment to the allowance for loan losses as of the first reporting period in which the new standard is effective, but cannot yet estimate the magnitude of the one-time adjustment or the overall impact of the new guidance on the </font><font style="display: inline;">Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In August 2016, the FASB issued accounting standards update 2016-15, Statement of Cash Flows. This update addresses eight specific cash flow issues with the objective of reducing the existing diversity in practice of how certain cash receipts and cash payments are presented and classified in the statement of cash flows. The amendments in this update are effective for fiscal years and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2017; however early adoption is permitted. Management is currently in the process of evaluating the impact of the update on the Company&#x2019;s statement of cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent:28.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In January 2017, the FASB issued accounting standards update 2017-04, Simplifying the Test for Goodwill Impairment. The provisions of the update eliminate the existing second step of the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">g</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">oodwill impairment test which provides for the allocation of reporting unit fair value amongst existing assets and liabilities, with the net leftover amount representing the implied fair value of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">g</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">oodwill. In replacement of the existing </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">g</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">oodwill impairment rule, the update will provide that impairment should be recognized as the excess if any of the reporting unit&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">g</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">oodwill over the fair value of the reporting unit. Under the provisions of this update the amount of the impairment is limited to the carrying value of the reporting unit&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">g</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">oodwill. </font><font style="display: inline;">For public business entities that are SEC filers the amendments of the update will become effective in fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2020.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.35pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.7pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">(z</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Reclassifications</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 49.65pt;text-indent: -27.35pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Certain reclassifications of prior year balances have been made to conform to the current year presentation. These reclassifications had no impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">3</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Business Combination</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On March 16, 2016, the Company entered into an Agreement and Plan of Reorganization (the &#x201C;Merger Agreement&#x201D;) with Home State, </font><font style="display: inline;">parent company of Home State Bank, </font><font style="display: inline;">a Colorado state chartered bank headquartered in Loveland, Colorado whereby Home State would merge into the Company. The transaction closed on September 8, 2016 with an aggregate transaction value of </font><font style="display: inline;">$152,478,000</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Merger Agreement provided that, subject to certain conditions, Home State shareholders would receive </font><font style="display: inline;">6,533,756</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of Company voting common stock valued at </font><font style="display: inline;">$117,477,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> based on the Company&#x2019;s closing stock price on September 8, 2016 of </font><font style="display: inline;">$17.98</font><font style="display: inline;">, in addition to </font><font style="display: inline;">$35,001,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> in cash. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The transaction enhance</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company&#x2019;s balance sheet </font><font style="display: inline;">liquidity and </font><font style="display: inline;">support</font><font style="display: inline;">ed</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company&#x2019;s objective of serving the banking needs of</font><font style="display: inline;"> northern Colorado</font><font style="display: inline;"> business and consumer customers</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Home State&#x2019;s results of operations have been included in the Company&#x2019;s results of operati</font><font style="display: inline;">ons beginning September 9, 2016;</font><font style="display: inline;"> however, it is </font><font style="display: inline;">impractical</font><font style="display: inline;"> to provide separate information on Home State&#x2019;s revenues and income subsequent to September 8, 2016 due to changes in the consolidated balance sheet. Pre-tax merger expenses of </font><font style="display: inline;">$6,259,000</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">were included in the Company&#x2019;s results of operations for the </font><font style="display: inline;">year ended December 31</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2016. </font><font style="display: inline;">The</font><font style="display: inline;"> pre-tax merger expenses incurred </font><font style="display: inline;">during 2016 consisted of</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$1,915,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> in salaries and employe</font><font style="display: inline;">e benefits expense and </font><font style="display: inline;">$4,344,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> in other general and administrative expense. In addition to merger-related costs recognized as expense, the Company incurred debt-issuance and sto</font><font style="display: inline;">ck-issuance costs of </font><font style="display: inline;">$830,000</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and </font><font style="display: inline;">$834,000</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively, </font><font style="display: inline;">during the year ended</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">December 31</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2016. Debt-issuance costs were recorded as a reduction to subordinated debentures and stock-issuance costs were recorded as a reduction to additional paid in capital on the Company&#x2019;s balance sheet. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill of </font><font style="display: inline;">$56,404,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> was recognized in the transaction and represents expected synergies and cost savings resulting from combining the operations of Home State with </font><font style="display: inline;">those of </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company. Due to the tax-free structure of the transaction, </font><font style="display: inline;">the recognized </font><font style="display: inline;">goodwill </font><font style="display: inline;">wa</font><font style="display: inline;">s not deductible for tax purposes. The fair values of assets acquired and liabilities assumed at acquisition </font><font style="display: inline;">were subjected to limited measurement period adjustments in the fourth quarter 2016 as a result of </font><font style="display: inline;">receipt of final valuations</font><font style="display: inline;">, with the net impact of these changes offset by a </font><font style="display: inline;">$256,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> increase in </font><font style="display: inline;">g</font><font style="display: inline;">oodwill</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">These adjustments included changes in the acquired fair value of investments, premises and equipment, other assets and liabilities, and the related impact to deferred income taxes. Impacts to income and expense recognized in the fourth quarter 2016 related to adjustments to the fair value of acquired assets and liabilities were not material.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The fair value of net assets acquired includes fair value adjustments to certain loans that were considered impaired as of the acquisition date. The fair value adjustments were determined using discounted expected cash flows. Acquired loans that evidence credit deterioration since origination, for which the acquirer does not expect to collect all contractual cash flows are designated as PCI upon acquisition. The gross contractual amount of loans identified as PCI as of the acquisition date totaled </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$2,834,000,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> contractual cash flows not expected to be collected as of acquisition date on these PCI loans totaled </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$531,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, representing </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">18.7%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of their contractual balance. Additionally, PCI loans had an interest rate fair value adjustment of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$195,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> bringing the net fair value to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$2,108,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> as of September 8, 2016. Cash flows on PCI loans cannot be reliably estimated and as a result these loans have been designated as nonaccrual. Loans that were not designated PCI at acquisition had a fair value of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$443,421,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and a contractual balance of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$458,014,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> as of September 8, 2016. The credit component of the fair value adjustment on non-PCI loans as of acquisition totaled </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$8,358,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, representing </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1.8%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of their contractual balances. No allowance for loan losses related to acquired loans was brought over as a result of the Home State transaction.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">In determining whether or not there is an OTTI for a security, management considers many factors, including: (i)&nbsp;the length of time for which and the extent to which the security&#x2019;s fair value has been less than cost, (ii)&nbsp;the financial condition and near-term prospects of the security&#x2019;s issuer, (iii)&nbsp;whether the decline in the security&#x2019;s value was affected by macroeconomic conditions, and (iv)&nbsp;whether the Company intends to sell the security and whether it is more likely than not that the Company will be required to sell the security before a recovery in its fair value. The assessment of whether an OTTI exists involves a high degree of subjectivity and judgment and is based on the information available to management at a particular point in time. T</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">here were </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">no</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> accumulated credit losses on any of the Company&#x2019;s securities as of December 31, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">At December 31, 2016, there were </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">271</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> individual securities in an unrealized loss position, including </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">10</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> individual securities that had been in a continuous unrealized loss position for 12 months or longer. Management has evaluated these securities in addition to the remaining </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">261</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> securities in an unrealized loss position and has determined that the decline in value since their purchase dates was primarily attributable to fluctuations in market interest rates and does not reflect a decline in the underlying issuers&#x2019; ability to repay. Management determined that the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">de</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">crease in the number of securities in an unrealized loss position in excess of 12 months from </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">43</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> securities at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2015 to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">10</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> securities at December 31, 2016 was primarily attributable to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">the repositioning of the Company&#x2019;s investment portfolio following the Home State transaction in addition to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">the timing of interest rate fluctuations. The total number of securities in an unrealized loss position increased from </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">88</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> individual securities at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2015</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> to 271 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">securities at December 31, 2016. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">At December 31, 2016 the Company did not intend to sell, and did not consider it likely that it would be required to sell, any</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> of these securities prior to recovery in their fair value.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">The </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">Company&#x2019;s unrated and rated municipal bond securities, along with the Company&#x2019;s other rated investment securities, are subject to an annual internal review process that management has historically performed in the fourth quarter. In addition, management considers any interim information reasonably made available to it that would prompt the need </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">for more frequent review. 			<font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">At </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">December 31, 2015, there were </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">88</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> individual securities in an unrealized loss position, including </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">43</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> individual securities that had been in a continuous unrealized loss position for 12 months or longer. Management evaluated these securities in addition to the remaining </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">45</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> securities in an unrealized loss position and determined that the decline in value since their purchase dates was primarily attributable to fluctuations in market interest rates and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">did</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;"> not reflect a decline in the underlying issuers&#x2019; ability to repay. At December 31, 2015 the Company did not intend to sell, and did not consider it likely that it would be required to sell</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">, any of these securities prior to recovery in their fair value</font><font style="display: inline;color:#231F20;">.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s additional disclosures relating to loans and the allowance for loan losses are broken out into two subsets, portfolio segment and class. The portfolio segment level is defined as the level where financing receivables are aggregated in developing the Company&#x2019;s systematic method for calculating its allowance for loan losses. The class level is the second level at which credit information is presented and represents the categorization of financing related receivables at a slightly less aggregated level than the portfolio segment level. Because data presented according to class is dependent upon the underlying purpose of the loan, whereas loan data organized by portfolio segment is determined by the loan&#x2019;s underlying collateral, disclosures broken out by portfolio segment versus class may not be in agreement. </font><font style="display: inline;">The disclosures in this footnote include both Non-PC</font><font style="display: inline;">I and PCI loans. As of December&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">31,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">2016 PCI loans acquired in the Home State transaction are not considered material and as a result separate PCI disclosures are not included.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">2016, 2015 and 2014, respectively. The income recognized on nonaccrual loans prior to impairment during 2016, 2015 and 2014 was </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$163,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$90,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$5,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> respectively. During 2016 and 2015 </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$332,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$118,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of cash basis interest income was recognized on a nonaccrual loan that was moved to accruing status in the third quarter of 2016. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">With the exception of cash-basis interest income, the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$2,291,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$666,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> in interest income recognized on impaired loans during 2016 and 2015 is primarily comprised of interest income recognized on performing TDRs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">The Company categorizes loans into risk categories based on relevant information about the ability of a particular borrower to service its debt, such as: current financial information, historical payment experience, credit documentation, public information, and current economic trends, among other factors. The Company uses the following definitions for risk ratings, which are consistent with the definitions used in supervisory guidance:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Substandard</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">. Loans classified as substandard are inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral, if any, pledged to secure the loan. Loans so classified have a well-defined weakness or weaknesses that jeopardize the collection of the debt. They are characterized by the distinct possibility that the Company will sustain some loss if the deficiencies are not corrected.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Doubtful</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">. Loans classified as doubtful have all the weaknesses inherent in those classified as substandard, with the added characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, highly questionable and improbable.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">Loans not meeting the criteria above are considered to be non-classified loans. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

Securities sold under agreements to repurchase are reflected at the amount of cash received in connection with the transaction. The Company may be required to provide additional collateral based on the fair value of the underlying security. The securities sold under agreements to repurchase are collateralized by government agency and mortgage-backed securities held by the Company, which had carrying values of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$42,825,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$29,059,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> at December 31, 2016 and 2015, respectively.</font>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">In April 2004, a predecessor to the Company formed CenBank Statutory Trust III and the trust completed an offering of </font><font style="display: inline;">$15,000,000,</font><font style="display: inline;"> LIBOR plus </font><font style="display: inline;">2.65%</font><font style="display: inline;"> Cumulative TruPS, which are guaranteed by the Company. The trust also issued common securities to the predecessor of the Company and used the net proceeds from the offering to purchase </font><font style="display: inline;">$15,464,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> in principal amount of floating rate Debentures issued by the predecessor. The Company assumed the predecessor&#x2019;s obligations relating to such securities upon the acquisition of the predecessor. Interest is paid quarterly and is distributed to the holders of the TruPS. These Debentures were unsecured, ranked junior and were subordinate in right of payment to all senior debt of the Company. The TruPS were subject to mandatory redemption upon repayment of the Debentures. The Company had the right, subject to events of default, to defer payments of interest on the Debentures at any time by extending the interest payment period for a period not exceeding </font><font style="display: inline;">60</font><font style="display: inline;"> consecutive months with respect to each deferral period, provided that no extension period could extend beyond the redemption or maturity date of the Debentures. The Debentures mature on April 15, 2034 and are callable on each quarterly payment date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In June 2003, a predecessor to the Company formed Guaranty Capital Trust III and the trust completed an offering of </font><font style="display: inline;">$10,000,000,</font><font style="display: inline;"> LIBOR plus </font><font style="display: inline;">3.10%</font><font style="display: inline;"> Cumulative TruPS, which are guaranteed by the Company. The trust also issued common securities to the predecessor of the Company and used the net proceeds from the offering to purchase </font><font style="display: inline;">$10,310,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> in principal amount of Debentures issued by the predecessor. The Company assumed the predecessor&#x2019;s obligations relating to such securities upon the acquisition of the predecessor. Interest is paid quarterly and is distributed to the holders of the TruPS. The other terms and condition of these Debentures are substantially similar to those described under the CenBank Statutory&nbsp;Trust&nbsp;III. The Debentures mature</font><font style="display: inline;"> on July 7, 2033 and are callable on each quarterly interest payment date. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the terms of each indenture pursuant to which the two respective Debentures were issued, the Company has the ability to defer interest on the Debentures for a period not exceeding </font><font style="display: inline;">60</font><font style="display: inline;"> consecutive months as long as it is in compliance with all covenants of the respective indenture. Such a deferral is not an event of default under each indenture and interest on the Debentures continues to accrue during the deferral period. </font><font style="display: inline;">No</font><font style="display: inline;"> interest is being deferred as of December 31, 2016.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company is not considered the primary beneficiary of the trusts </font><font style="display: inline;">that issued the TruPS </font><font style="display: inline;">(variable interest entities)</font><font style="display: inline;">;</font><font style="display: inline;"> therefore</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> the trusts are not consolidated in the Company&#x2019;s financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> the</font><font style="display: inline;">se</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">two D</font><font style="display: inline;">ebentures are shown as liabilit</font><font style="display: inline;">ies. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s investment in the common stock of each trust is included in other assets in the</font><font style="display: inline;"> Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">c</font><font style="display: inline;">onsolidated </font><font style="display: inline;">b</font><font style="display: inline;">alance </font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">heets</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

This third issuance of </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">40,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> fixed-to-floating rate subordinated Debentures yield </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">5.75%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and are due July 20, 2026. 			<font style="display: inline;">Although the securities issued by each of the trusts are not included as a component of stockholders&#x2019; equity in the consolidated </font><font style="display: inline;">balance sheets, they are treated as capital for regulatory purposes. Any amount that exceeds </font><font style="display: inline;">25</font><font style="display: inline;">% qualifies as Tier 2 capital. At both December</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, and December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">, the full $</font><font style="display: inline;">25,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the TruPS qualified as Tier 1 capital.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The </font><font style="display: inline;">$40,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> from July 2016 issuance qualifies for inclusion in Tier 2 capital. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2016</font><font style="display: inline;">, the rates on the fixed rate commitments to extend credit </font><font style="display: inline;">ranged </font><font style="display: inline;">from </font><font style="display: inline;">1.95</font><font style="display: inline;">% to </font><font style="display: inline;">6.75</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A c</font><font style="display: inline;">ommitment to extend credit </font><font style="display: inline;">is an</font><font style="display: inline;"> agreement to lend to a customer as long as there is no violation of any</font><font style="display: inline;"> condition established in the </font><font style="display: inline;">underlying </font><font style="display: inline;">contract. Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and may require payment of a fee. Several of the commitments may expire without being drawn upon.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Therefore, the total commitment amounts do not necessarily represent future cash requirements.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Off-balance sheet risk to credit loss exists up to the face amount of these instruments, although material losses are not anticipated. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A c</font><font style="display: inline;">ommitment to extend credit under </font><font style="display: inline;">an </font><font style="display: inline;">overdraft protection agreement </font><font style="display: inline;">is a </font><font style="display: inline;">commitment for </font><font style="display: inline;">a &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">possible future extension of credit to </font><font style="display: inline;">an </font><font style="display: inline;">existing deposit customer. These lines of credit are uncollateralized and usually do not contain a specified maturity date and may not be drawn upon to the total extent to which the </font><font style="display: inline;">Bank</font><font style="display: inline;"> is committed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued by the </font><font style="display: inline;">Bank</font><font style="display: inline;"> to guarantee the performance of </font><font style="display: inline;">a customer to a third party. The</font><font style="display: inline;">se letters of credit are primarily issued to support public and private borrowing arrangements. </font><font style="display: inline;">A majority of</font><font style="display: inline;"> letters of credit issued have expiration dates within </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> year.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The credit risk involved in issuing letters of credit is essentially the same as that involved in extending loan facilities to customers. The </font><font style="display: inline;">Bank</font><font style="display: inline;"> holds collat</font><font style="display: inline;">eral supporting the</font><font style="display: inline;">se commitments if deemed necessary.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent: -22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Substantially all employees are eligible to participate in the Company&#x2019;s 401(k) plan. Employees may contribute up to </font><font style="display: inline;">100%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of their compensation subject to certain limits based on federal tax laws. The Company makes matching contributions equal to a specified percentage of the employee&#x2019;s compensation as defined by the plan. For years ended December&nbsp;31, 2016, 2015 and 2014, matching contributions to the 401(k) plan </font><font style="display: inline;">were </font><font style="display: inline;">$615,000</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$503,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">$471,000</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Stock-Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the Company&#x2019;s Incentive Plan, which expired by its terms on April 4, 2015, the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors had authority to grant stock-based compensation awards prior to the plan&#x2019;s expiration. Under the 2015 Plan, which was approved by the Company&#x2019;s stockholders at the May 5, 2015 annual meeting, the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors maintains the authority to grant stock-based compensation awards to nonemployee directors, key employees, consultants and prospective employees.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Stock-based compensation awards issuable under the Incentive Plan include the grant of stock-based compensation awards in the form of options, restricted stock awards, restricted stock unit awards, performance stock awards, stock appreciation rights and other equity based awards. Likewise, the Incentive Plan provided for, and the 2015 Plan provides, that eligible participants may be granted shares of Company common stock that are subject to forfeiture until the grantee vests in the stock award based on the established conditions, which may include service conditions, established performance measures</font><font style="display: inline;"> or both.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Prior to the vesting of stock awards that are subject to a service vesting condition, each grantee has the rights of a stockholder with respect to voting the shares of stock represented by the award. The grantee is not entitled to dividend rights with respect to the shares of stock until vesting occurs. Prior to vesting of the stock awards with performance vesting conditions, each grantee has the rights of a stockholder with respect to voting of the shares of stock represented by the award. The recipient is generally not entitled to dividend rights with respect to unvested shares. Other than the stock awards with service and performance-based vesting conditions, no other grants have</font><font style="display: inline;"> been made under the Incentive Plan</font><font style="display: inline;"> or 2015 Plan</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the provisions of the 2015 Plan and the Incentive Plan grants of stock-based compensation awards of </font><font style="display: inline;">935,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">1,700,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares, respectively, were authorized, subject to adjustments upon the occurrence of certain events. As of </font><font style="display: inline;">December&nbsp;31</font><font style="display: inline;">,&nbsp;2016 there </font><font style="display: inline;">were </font><font style="display: inline;">1</font><font style="display: inline;">78,513</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">334,674 </font><font style="display: inline;">outstanding</font><font style="display: inline;"> awards under the 2015 Plan and the Incentive Plan, respectively. As of December 31, 2016 there were </font><font style="display: inline;">728,305</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">shares remaining available for grant under the 2015 Plan. As of December 31, 2015 there were </font><font style="display: inline;">21,846</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">568,909</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">outstanding</font><font style="display: inline;"> awards under the 2015 Plan and the Incentive Plan, respectively</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and </font><font style="display: inline;">913,154</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares </font><font style="display: inline;">remaining available for grant under the 2015 Plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Of the </font><font style="display: inline;">513,187</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares represented by unvested awards at </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2016, approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">494,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares are expected to vest. At </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2016, there were </font><font style="display: inline;">315,966</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of restricted stock outstanding that were subject to a performance condition</font><font style="display: inline;">. As of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> management expects that approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">307,000</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">of these shares will vest and that the remaining shares will expire unvested. The performance shares that are expected</font><font style="display: inline;"> to vest relate to awards granted to various key employees from February 2014 through </font><font style="display: inline;">November</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2016. The vesting of these performance shares is contingent upon meeting certain return on average asset performance measures. The performance-based shares awarded in 2014, 2015 and 2016 each include a &#x201C;threshold&#x201D; and &#x201C;target&#x201D; performance level, with vesting determined based on where actual performance falls in relation to the numeric range represented by these performance criteria</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 2016 management expected that all of the performance awards made in 2014, 2015 and 2016 not forfeited from a failure by the grantee to provide the requisite service will vest, </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent: -22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">18</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Fair value is the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date. There are three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair values:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 1 - Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 2 - Significant other observable inputs other than Level 1 prices such as quoted prices in markets that are not active, quoted prices for similar assets, or other inputs that are observable, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the asset.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 3 - Significant unobservable inputs that reflect a reporting entity&#x2019;s own assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A financial instrument&#x2019;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement. Transfers of financial instruments between levels within the fair value hierarchy are recognized on the date management determines that the underlying circumstances or assumptions have changed. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Fair values of our securities are determined through the utilization of evaluated pricing models that vary by asset class and incorporate available market information (Level 2). The evaluated pricing models apply available information, as applicable, through processes such as benchmark curves, benchmarking of like securities, sector groupings, and matrix pricing to prepare evaluations. These models assess interest rate impact, develop prepayment </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">114</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

Due to the lack of ratings available on these securities, management determined that a relationship to other benchmark quoted securities was unobservable and as a result these securities should be classified as Level 3 (Level 3 inputs). The valuation of the Company&#x2019;s Level 3 bonds is highly sensitive to changes in unobservable inputs.</font>
		</p>

The fair value of interest rate swaps are determined using the market standard methodology of netting the discounted future fixed cash payments (or receipts) and the discounted expected variable cash receipts (or payments). The variable cash receipts (or payments) are based on the expectation of future interest rates (forward curves) derived from observed market interest rate curves (Level 2 inputs). The Company considers the value of the swaps to be sensitive to fluctuations in interest rates.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:6pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The fair value of a financial instrument is the current amount that would be exchanged</font><font style="display: inline;"> between willing parties, other than in a forced liquidation. Fair value is best determined based upon quoted market prices.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;H</font><font style="display: inline;">owever, in many instances, there are no quoted market prices for the Company&#x2019;s various financial instruments.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">In cases where quoted market prices are not available, fair values are based on estimates using present value or other valuation techniques.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Those techniques are significantly affected by the assumptions used, including the discount rate and estimates of future cash flows.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Accordingly, the fair value estimates may not be realized in an immediate settlement of the instrument. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
