			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">GUARANTY BANCORP AND SUBSIDIARIES</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			<a href="#TableofContents"><font style="display: inline;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Certain financial instruments and all nonfinancial instruments are excluded from the disclosure requirements.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Therefore, the aggregate fair value amounts presented may not necessarily represent the underlying fair value of the Company.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The following methods and assumptions </font><font style="display: inline;">are</font><font style="display: inline;"> used by the Company in estimating fair value disclosures for financial instruments:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:22pt;"><p style="width:22pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 21.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;;"> (a)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 40.5pt;text-indent: -18pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">The carrying amounts of cash and short-term instruments approximate fair values</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;"> (Level 1)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;text-indent:4.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:22pt;"><p style="width:22pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 21.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;;"> (b)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Securities and Bank Stocks </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">Fair values for securities available for sale and held to maturity are generally </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">determined through the utilization of evaluated pricing models that vary by asset class and incorporate available market information (Level 2). The evaluated pricing models apply available information, as applicable, through processes such as benchmark curves, benchmarking of like securities, sector groupings, and matrix pricing to prepare evaluations. These models assess interest rate impact, develop prepayment scenarios and take into account market conventions.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;"> For positions that are not traded in active markets or are subject to transfer restrictions (i.e., bonds valued with Level 3 inputs), management uses a combination of reviews of the underlying financial statements, appraisals and management&#x2019;s judgment regarding credit quality and intent to sell in order to determine the value of the bond.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">It is not practical to determine the fair value of bank stocks due to restrictions placed on the transferability of </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">FHLB stock, Federal Reserve Bank stock and Bankers&#x2019; Bank of the West stock. These three stocks comprise the majority of the balance of the Company&#x2019;s bank stocks</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">c</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Loans Held for Investment </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For variable</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> rate loans that reprice frequently and with no significant change in credit risk, fair values are based on carrying values</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> (Level 3)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. Fair values for other loans (e.g., commercial real estate and investment property mortgage loans, commercial loans) are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses, using interest rates currently being offered for loans with similar terms to borrowers of similar credit quality</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> (Level 3)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Impaired loans are valued at the lower of cost or fair value</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> when specific reserves are attributed to these loans because the present value of expected cash flows or the net realizable value of collateral is less than the impaired loan&#x2019;s recorded investment</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> The methods utilized to estimate the fair value of loans do not necessarily represent an exit price.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">d</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Loans</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"> Held for Sale</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">L</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">oans</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> held for sale are carried at the lower of cost or fair value, with fair value determined by the sales price agreed upon in negotiations with the purchaser (Level 1). </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">e</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Deposits </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The fair values </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">demand deposits (e.g., interest and non-interest checking, passbook savings, and certain types of money market accounts) are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date (i.e., their carrying amount)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> (Level 2)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The carrying amounts of variable rate, fixed-term money market accounts and certificates of deposit approximate their fair values at the reporting date</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> (Level 2)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. Fair values for fixed rate certificates of deposit are estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that applies interest rates currently being offered on certificates to a schedule of aggregated expected monthly maturities on time deposits</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> (Level 2)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">g</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Long-term Borrowings </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.35pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The fair values </font><font style="display: inline;">of the Company&#x2019;s long-term borro</font><font style="display: inline;">wings are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses based on the Company&#x2019;s current incremental borrowing rates for similar types of borrowing arrangements</font><font style="display: inline;"> (Level 2)</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">h</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Subordinated Debentures </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.35pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The fair values of the Company&#x2019;s Subordinated Debentures are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses based on the Company&#x2019;s current incremental borrowing rates for similar types of borrowing arrangements</font><font style="display: inline;"> (Level 3)</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">i</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Accrued Interest Receivable/Payable</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The carrying amounts of accrued interest approximate fair </font><font style="display: inline;">value (Level 2).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 45pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">j</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Interest Rate Swaps, net</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The fair value of interest rate swaps are determined using the market standard methodology of netting the discounted future fixed cash payments (or receipts) and the discounted expected variable cash receipts (or payments).&nbsp;The variable cash receipts (or payments) are based on the expectation of future interest rates (forward curves) derived from observed market interest rate curves (Level 2). </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">k</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Off-balance Sheet Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.3pt;text-indent:27.2pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Fair values for off-balance sheet, credit-related financial instruments are bas</font><font style="display: inline;">ed on fees currently charged to </font><font style="display: inline;">enter into similar agreements, taking into account the remaining terms of the agreements and the</font><font style="display: inline;"> counterparties&#x2019; credit standing. The fair value of commitments is not material</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">(1</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">9</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Derivatives and Hedging Activities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company is exposed to certain risks arising from both its business operations and economic conditions. The Company principally manages its exposures to a wide variety of business and operational risks through management of its core business activities. The Company utilizes derivative financial instruments to assist in the management of interest rate risk, primarily helping to secure long-term borrowing rates. Specifically, the Company enters into derivative financial instruments to manage exposures that arise from business activities that result in the payment or receipt of future known and uncertain cash amounts, the value of which are determined by interest rates. The Company&#x2019;s derivative financial instruments are used to manage differences in the amount, timing and duration of the Company&#x2019;s known or expected cash payments or receipts principally related to certain variable-rate borrowings. The Company does not use derivatives for trading or speculative purposes.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s objectives in using interest rate derivatives are to add stability and predictability to interest expense and to manage the Company&#x2019;s exposure to interest rate movements. To accomplish this objective, the Company primarily uses interest rate swaps as part of its interest rate risk management strategy. For hedges of the Company&#x2019;s variable-rate borrowings, interest rate swaps designated as cash flow hedges involve the receipt of variable amounts from a counterparty in exchange for the Company making fixed payments. As of </font>

				</td>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:02.02%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #CCEEFF;height:10.50pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0.05pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;overflow: hidden;font-size:0pt;">
						&nbsp;</p>
				</td>
			</tr>
		</table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The effective portion of changes in the fair value of derivatives designated and that qualify as cash flow hedges is recorded in AOCI and is subsequently reclassified into earnings in the period that the hedged forecasted transaction affects earnings. The ineffective portion of the change in fair value of the derivatives is recognized directly in earnings. The Company&#x2019;s cash flow hedges are used to hedge the forecasted variable cash outflows associated with forecasted issuances of FHLB advances. During 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6, </font><font style="display: inline;">201</font><font style="display: inline;">5, and 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, the income statement effect of hedge ineffectiveness was not material.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Amounts reported in AOCI related to derivatives will be reclassified to interest expense as interest payments are made on the Company&#x2019;s variable-rate liabilities. Management expects that, during the next 12 months </font><font style="display: inline;">approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$790,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> will be</font><font style="display: inline;"> reclassified from AOCI into interest expense. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company executes interest rate swaps with commercial banking customers to facilitate their respective risk management strategies. Those interest rate swaps are simultaneously hedged by offsetting interest rate swaps that the Company executes with another third party, such that the Company minimizes its net risk exposure resulting from such transactions. As the interest rate swaps associated with this program do not meet the strict hedge accounting requirements, changes in the fair value of both the customer swaps and the offsetting swaps are recognized directly in earnings. The impact of these customer interest rate swaps on the Company&#x2019;s financial statements was not material for any periods covered by this report. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">(</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">21</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 16pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Regulatory Capital Matters</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 22.5pt;text-indent: -22.5pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Holding Company and the Bank are subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies. Failure to meet minimum capital requirements can initiate certain mandatory and possibly additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements. Under capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, the Company must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of their assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices. The Company&#x2019;s capital amounts and classification are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weighting, and other factors.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Current risk-based regulatory capital standards generally require banks and bank holding companies to maintain a ratio of Common Equity Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets of at least 4.50%, </font><font style="display: inline;">a ratio of </font><font style="display: inline;">Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets of at least 6.00%, a ratio of Tier 1 capital to average total assets (leverage ratio) of at least 4.00% and a ratio of total capital (which includes Tier 1 capital plus certain forms of subordinated debt, a portion of the allowance for loan and lease losses, and preferred stock) to risk-weighted assets of at least 8.00%. </font><font style="display: inline;">However, u</font><font style="display: inline;">nder the final rule on Enhanced Regulatory Capital Standards, commonly referred to as Basel III, which became effective in the first quarter 2015, a capital conservation buffer of 2.5%, comprised of Common Equity Tier 1 was established above the regulatory minimum capital requirement. The capital conservation buffer phase-in period began January 1, 2016 and will become fully effective on January 1, 2019. A fully phased-in capital conservation buffer is included in the table below. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Management believes that the Holding Company and the Bank met all capital adequacy requirements to which they are subject.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
